L&T shall be a professionally-managed Indian multinational, committed to total customer satisfaction and enhancing shareholder value.
L&T-ites shall be an innovative, entrepreneurial and empowered team constantly creating value and attaining global benchmarks.

structure.title: Dear Shareholders,
structure.summary: The text is a Chairman and Managing Director's message to shareholders for 2024-25, highlighting a transformative year amid global geopolitical, technological, climate, and supply chain disruptions. It reports standout company performance through digital adoption, project execution, and sustainable solutions, with a robust order book positioning L&T for leadership. The message covers diversified portfolio strengths, monitoring of global uncertainties with optimism about the Middle East and domestic Indian infrastructure support, and private investment trends. It emphasizes safety via 'Mission Zero Harm' and 'L.I.F.E.', including AR/VR training and a reward-penalty system. Group business highlights include infrastructure milestones: Mumbai Metro Line 3, Riyadh Metro, India's longest railway tunnel, and Saudi solar projects. The document also lists corporate sections like Management Discussion, Integrated Report, and Financial Statements.

structure.title: Chairman's Statement: Growth, Safety, and Diversified Business
structure.summary: The page is a Chairman’s Statement covering several short sections. It emphasizes a well-diversified portfolio and agile business model, with growth monitoring global economic uncertainties, optimism about Middle East infrastructure investment, and domestic expectations of government and private infrastructure spending. It highlights safety through 'Mission Zero Harm' and 'L.I.F.E.' frameworks, enhanced supervision, AR/VR training, and a Reward and Penalty System linking safety to incentives and bonuses. The Group Businesses section describes resilience, innovation, and a diversified portfolio across infrastructure, energy, manufacturing, services, and new-age ventures, reinforced by core values and a culture of continuous learning for inclusive growth.

structure.title: 1. Infrastructure
structure.summary: The text highlights the company's infrastructure legacy in large-scale EPC projects, with milestones including Mumbai Metro Line 3 and Riyadh Metro inaugurations, a breakthrough in India's longest railway tunnel under RVNL, and commissioning of solar PV projects (1.6 GW Sudair, 700 MW Ar Rass, 800 MW DEWA Phase VI, 1.4 GW Al Kahfah, 2 GW Ar Rass-2). It also notes completion of the National Cricket Academy and government medical colleges, progress on thermal power projects (Khurja and Buxar), expressway stretches, segmentation of Hydrocarbon business into Onshore and Offshore with a major Middle East order, and water supply projects benefiting over two million people.

structure.title: 2. Energy
structure.summary: The text covers the company's energy transition, detailing four business verticals: Hydrocarbon Onshore, Hydrocarbon Offshore, CarbonLite Solutions, and Green & Clean Energy. It highlights CarbonLite's focus on carbon capture, nuclear turbine islands, pumped storage, and BTG packages. Green & Clean Energy builds a sustainable ecosystem. Key projects include a 9 MMTPA CDU-VDU for HPCL and a 90 MW floating solar project. The Hi-Tech Manufacturing section notes milestones: commissioning the CDU-VDU, completing the first offshore decommissioning in Tapti Gas Fields, and achievements of the Heavy Engineering and Precision Engineering divisions, including commercial operation, heavy reactor deliveries, a Saudi filter vessel order, and contributions to Aatmanirbhar Bharat (Zorawar tank, NGHHTS, Fleet Support Ships) and an ISRO partnership.

nodes.title: Engineering Solutions for the New Age
nodes.summary: The text covers L&T's engineering solutions across three areas. (a) Digital and AI Transformation: L&T's early adoption of automation, IoT, and digital sensors for connected construction sites; custom applications; launch of L&T Cognitive Services (L&TCS), an enterprise AI platform for predictive analytics, improving quality, safety, revenue, efficiency, inventory, manpower, and cost; establishment of Digital Energy Solutions (DES) offering proprietary software for renewable integration, hybrid energy management, substation automation, grid-edge solutions, and cybersecurity; and the Cybersecurity Council for data protection. (b) Climate Resilience and Green Business: response to extreme weather risks; expertise in clean energy, mobility, water, sanitation, and green infrastructure; entry into Green Hydrogen (electrolyser manufacturing underway) and Small Modular Reactors (US DOE approval for technology transfer); land secured for Green Hydrogen/Ammonia manufacturing; EPC capabilities; Green Energy Council think tank; green buildings (15.6 million sq.ft. in FY25, 57.6 million cumulative); renewable energy portfolio (26.9 GWp total, 4.3 GWp commissioned, 20 GWp pipeline); 12.8 GWh BESS under execution; railway electrification (419 track km); equipment for renewable diesel and biofuels. (c) Sustainability: vision 'For A Better World'; ESG initiatives; targets of Water Neutrality by 2035 and Carbon Neutrality by 2040; Water Technology Centre innovations; Zero Liquid Discharge systems at 16 campuses; plastic-free campus at Hazira; Unnati watershed programme expansion.

nodes.title: Key Developments
nodes.summary: The section covers key corporate developments: an S&P and Fitch ratings upgrade to 'BBB+', expansion of Precision Engineering & Systems, rebranding Power EPC as CarbonLite Solutions, and business reclassification for autonomy. People initiatives include innovation culture, 7.95 lakh learning hours, and 'Great Place to Work' certification. Diversity efforts feature 9.06% female representation and paid menstrual leave. CSR impacts 1.9 million people through healthcare, education, watershed, and STEM programs. Governance emphasizes ethics, transparency, and compliance. Future positioning highlights strengths in infrastructure, energy transition, and manufacturing aligned with Lakshya 2031, with gratitude to stakeholders.

nodes.title: People Powering Progress
nodes.summary: The text covers key developments: a ratings upgrade to 'BBB+' by S&P and Fitch, two notches above India's sovereign rating; expansion of Precision Engineering & Systems into industrial electronics and collaboration with tech start-ups; rebranding of Power EPC as CarbonLite Solutions focusing on carbon capture and biofuels; and reclassification of businesses to enhance autonomy and growth, including carving out Renewables EPC and consolidating Green EPC and Gas-to-Power under L&T Green & Clean Energy. It also highlights people initiatives: a culture of innovation, 7.95 lakh learning hours, digital champions, recognition culture, and second consecutive 'Great Place to Work' certification.

nodes.title: Driving Inclusion Through Transformation
nodes.summary: The Company's evolution into a technology-led conglomerate has renewed focus on its Diversity & Inclusion agenda, with growing participation of women in engineering and non-engineering roles advancing workplace equity, operational efficiency, and innovation. Committed to an inclusive work environment, the Company invests in career-enabling initiatives and women-centric infrastructure, staying on track for the 'Lakshya' goal of 10% women representation by 2026. As of March 31, 2025, permanent female employees numbered 4,758, comprising 9.06% of the total workforce. Additionally, effective April 1, 2025, the Company introduced an industry-first one day of paid menstrual leave per month for women employees, reflecting an empathetic approach to employee well-being and supporting unique health needs.

nodes.title: Giving Back to Society
nodes.summary: The company's CSR efforts focus on inclusive growth and stakeholder trust through healthcare, education, skill development, and water & sanitation, impacting 1.9 million people. The Integrated Community Development Programme strengthens rural communities. The Unnati watershed programme, since 2014 in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Tamil Nadu, has treated 44,856 hectares and benefited 30,092 households via check dams, trenches, and plantations, improving crops, fodder, and incomes, with Village Development Committees ensuring sustainability. The Jyoti STEM Education Programme bridges learning gaps in grades 6–8 in Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra using digital tools, robotics, and teacher training, benefiting 314 schools and 52,924 students in FY 2024–25, enhancing engagement and interest in maths and science. These initiatives demonstrate that sustainable business growth and social responsibility can go hand in hand.

nodes.title: Governance and Ethics
nodes.summary:
Governance and Ethics
The Company remains steadfast in its commitment to the highest standards of ethics, transparency and accountability across all its operations. Good governance is a must.
A robust governance framework is in place to ensure strict compliance with applicable laws, regulations and global best practices, including those pertaining to human rights and fair business conduct. This unwavering focus on ethical business practices reinforces stakeholder trust and supports the Company’s long-term, sustainable growth.

nodes.title: Positioned for the Future
nodes.summary: The text highlights the company's strategic positioning to seize opportunities amid global shifts, citing strengths in infrastructure, EPC projects, energy transition, hi-tech manufacturing, and technology-led execution. It notes alignment of all business verticals with a sustainable economy vision via the Lakshya 2031 strategic plan, a five-year roadmap. The speaker expresses gratitude to employees, customers, supply chain partners, the Government, Board members, and shareholders for their support and trust, and looks forward to continued support for excellence and sustainable growth, ending with 'Jai Hind!'.

nodes.title: Economy
nodes.summary: The text covers India's economic outlook for 2024-25, projecting 6.25-6.50% growth with sectoral breakdowns (agriculture ~4%, industry ~6%, services ~7%). It details inflation trends, noting easing CPI to 4.63% in FY 2024-25 from 5.35% prior, driven by core services and fuel, while food inflation remains firm. RBI's inflation forecast for FY 2025-26 is 4%. Monetary policy is discussed: repo rate held at 6.50% through April-December 2024, stance shifted to 'Neutral' in October 2024, CRR cut to 4.00% in December 2024, and repo rate reduced to 6.25% in February 2025. External trade shows stability with exports exceeding USD 800 billion (5.5% growth) and imports at USD 915 billion (6.8% growth). Rupee weakened ~5% against USD from October to mid-February amid volatility. FPI inflows were ~USD 20 billion in H1 but reversed to net outflows in H2; debt securities saw ~USD 15 billion inflows, equity outflows similar. Growth drivers include resilient consumption, government capital expenditure, high manufacturing capacity utilisation, healthy balance sheets, and rapid digitalisation. Risks are external: rising tariff barriers, supply chain issues, and geopolitical tensions.

nodes.title: Global Economy
nodes.summary: Global GDP grew 2.7% in 2024, with US growth at 2.8%, Eurozone at 0.8%, India at 6.5%, and China at 5%. Improving financial conditions, declining inflation, and partial de-escalation of conflicts marked the year. US risks shifted from inflation to growth due to tariffs and regulatory, immigration, and fiscal changes, creating monetary policy challenges; technology remains a bright spot with spending to exceed USD 2 trillion in 2025. Europe and UK remain fragile, but Germany's EUR 500 billion infrastructure fund could alter medium-term growth. China faces direct tariff impact and may use monetary easing and fiscal support. GCC continues infrastructure strengthening and oil & gas monetization amid transition to clean energy. Slowing global trade poses cost and productivity risks, but IT outsourcing remains resilient, with India's tech sector growing 5% in FY 2025-26 to over USD 300 billion. India is insulated and on track to become the third-largest economy, supported by demographics, investment, and reforms.

nodes.summary: L&T's Risk Management Framework addresses diverse risks across its global operations. The framework proactively identifies, assesses, and mitigates risks through Enterprise Risk Management processes overseen by the Chief Risk Officer and Board committees. Key risks are classified as operational, tactical, and strategic. Operational risks include project execution (workmen shortages, regulatory delays, supply chain disruptions, design changes), quality and safety, supply chain and vendor management, technology and cybersecurity, legal and contractual, logistics and infrastructure, black swan events, and manufacturing operations. Tactical risks cover market and industry (economic/policy, competition, end-market slowdown, credit facilities), geopolitical/country, sanctions and regulatory, and workforce/talent management. Mitigation strategies include diversification, digitalization, strict quality and safety protocols (ISO standards), robust cybersecurity, contractual negotiations, and talent development.

Audit mechanisms include statutory auditors, Corporate Audit Services (CAS), and third-party audits; CAS evaluates design and operating effectiveness, with annual audit plans reviewed by the Audit Committee and quarterly reporting of findings. A three-line model is described: business heads as first line, Corporate Internal Control as second line, and CAS as third line providing independent assurance. nodes.title: Risks and Concerns

nodes.title: Transportation Infrastructure
nodes.summary: The Transportation Infrastructure section covers turnkey EPC solutions across roads, bridges, railways, urban transit, and airports, organized into Roads, Bridges & Formations (RBF) and Railways (RBG) groups, plus an international unit and design centers. It details India's business environment with record NHAI and railway capital expenditures, policy momentum, and modernization initiatives. Major achievements include key orders like NAINA roads and Chennai Peripheral Ring Road, and completed projects such as MAGRP, MIEP, MKRP, MMRC 10C, and RRTS Delhi-Meerut. nodes.title: Overview
nodes.summary: The Transportation Infrastructure business provides turnkey EPC solutions for roads, runways, bridges, elevated corridors, railways, urban transit, and airports. It is divided into two Strategic Business Groups: Roads, Bridges & Formations (RBF) and Railways (RBG). RBF includes Roads & Runways (road infrastructure, airports, elevated corridors), Bridges (using advanced techniques), and Formations & Structure (railway civil works for DFC, HSR, urban rail). RBG includes Mainline (civil, trackwork, electrification, system integration for mainline, DFC, port/industrial rail links) and Metro (ballastless track, electrification, systems integration for MRTS, RRTS, semi-HSR, HSR). An International Business Unit focuses on ASEAN and Middle East opportunities in mainline and integrated systems for mass transit and HSR. Engineering Design Centres are in Mumbai, Faridabad, Chennai, with a Competency Development Centre in Kancheepuram and Workmen Training Centre in Ahmedabad. It also mentions precast slab track for Delhi–Meerut RRTS.

nodes.title: Heavy Civil Infrastructure

nodes.title: Overview
nodes.summary: The Heavy Civil Infrastructure business is an EPC leader in core civil infrastructure segments: Urban Transit (metros, semi/high-speed rail, tunnels), Hydel & Tunnels, Nuclear, Ports & Harbours, and Defence Infrastructure. It has a robust domestic presence, offers turnkey solutions, and gains competitive edge from in-house design, technical capabilities, fabrication facilities, training centres, skilled workforce, and advanced equipment. Urban Transit is executing metro packages in multiple cities and India's first HSR corridor, using advanced techniques and in-house fabricated equipment. Hydel & Tunnels offers turnkey solutions for dams, barrages, pumped storage, and irrigation projects across several states. Nuclear undertakes civil works for PHWR, LWR, and NDCT. Ports & Harbours specializes in greenfield ports, shipyards, and marine structures in four coastal states. Defence Infrastructure provides single-point EPC solutions, with subsidiary L&T GeoStructure pioneering ground engineering, foundation, and sophisticated foundation works.

nodes.title: Business Environment

It highlights metro rail expansion to over 1,000 km in 23 cities, with plans for 1,032 km more in 26 cities, and urban transit tunnels. Hydel focuses on pumped storage projects to meet COP26 goals of 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, with streamlined frameworks for private participation. Nuclear targets 100 GW by 2047 via the Nuclear Energy Mission, including SMRs with ₹20,000 crore allocated. Ports and harbours detail the Sagarmala programme's 800 projects and ₹30,000 crore budget for modernisation. Defence emphasizes capacity building and infrastructure upgrades. To address rapid urbanization, it is considering mass transit systems like Metro, Metro Lite, Metro Neo, and Personal Rapid Transit in Tier 1 and 2 cities as part of green mobility to cut carbon emissions. Supportive policies and incentives also create opportunities in hydro, nuclear, and pumped storage for sustainable energy transition.

nodes.title: Overview
nodes.summary: The Power Transmission & Distribution (PT&D) vertical is a major EPC player offering technology-driven, end-to-end solutions for clean, reliable electricity access across 30 countries. It provides integrated EPC and digital energy solutions from smart T&D networks to last-mile electrification, serving utilities, renewable developers, industrial and infrastructure customers. The business is organized into T&D and Digital Energy Solutions (DES). T&D covers turnkey substations up to 1,200 kV, FACTS devices, digital substations, EHV cables, overhead transmission lines with in-house tower manufacturing and testing, and power distribution EPC services. Geographically, it operates in India, Saudi Arabia, UAE, the Middle East, Africa, ASEAN, and CIS, with a strong track record. DES provides global consulting and digital solutions including hybrid energy management, automation, grid edge interconnection, and cybersecurity, enabling resilient systems in India, the Middle East, and the USA.

nodes.title: Water & Effluent Treatment

nodes.title: Overview

WET is structured into three verticals: Water & Wastewater (municipal and rural potable water and wastewater projects), Irrigation, Industrial & Infrastructure (mega/micro irrigation, industrial effluent treatment, plant water systems, smart city water infrastructure, and desalination), and Water International (complete water solutions in the Middle East and East Africa).

nodes.title: Minerals & Metals

nodes.title: Overview
nodes.summary: The Minerals & Metals business provides complete EPC solutions for mineral and metal sectors globally, covering engineering, procurement, manufacturing, supply, construction, erection, and commissioning from mineral processing to finished metals. It offers customized product solutions including mineral crushing equipment, surface miners, material handling equipment, high-speed railway construction equipment, steel plant machinery, port and shipyard cranes, and other critical equipment for mining, steel, ports, fertilizers, cement, and chemical plants. Backed by six decades of experience, in-house design, advanced manufacturing, and after-sales support, it has manufacturing centres in Kansbahal, Odisha (ISO 9001:2008 certified with CAE and simulation facilities) and Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, plus Engineering Design & Research Centres in Kolkata, Chennai, and Mumbai.

nodes.title: Business Environment
nodes.summary: The text covers the business environment for an M&M company. Domestically, India is the second-largest crude steel producer, with robust consumption driven by infrastructure, automotive, construction, and consumer goods; FY 2024-25 production and consumption forecasts are given. Government infrastructure focus drives metal demand. Lithium discoveries in Jammu & Kashmir and Rajasthan can reduce import dependence and support green mobility. Internationally, Middle East metallurgy investments are a focus due to land, low energy costs, solar potential, and European proximity; GCC diversification and mineral supply chain security create opportunities in process plants for iron and steel, aluminum, gold, phosphate, copper, and new-age metals. The product business outlook is positive due to infrastructure, urbanization, and industrial expansion. It pursues international opportunities, securing a European stacker reclaimer order and repeat African surface miner orders. Growth in crushing systems, surface miners, material handling, cranes, and steel plant equipment is driven by cement (6-7% CAGR, 40-45 MT capacity addition), mining, power, and steel (National Steel Policy 300 MTPA by 2030, 80 GW thermal capacity addition), construction (highway budget), and port sectors (Sagarmala, Maritime India Vision 2030, container traffic growth, shipyard cranes).

nodes.title: Major Achievements
nodes.summary: The text outlines major achievements in two sections. Major orders won include DRI and pellet plants in the UAE, freight handling facilities in the UAE, a first EPC order for a 2*8 MTPA pellet plant, a coke oven battery, an alumina refinery in Odisha, a tail gas treatment plant, and the largest order for material handling equipment. It also lists the Mansourah-Massarah Gold Project, the largest port crane order, and the largest order for torpedo ladle cars. Marquee projects commissioned cover a 3 MTPA alumina refinery, hot commissioning of a twin slab caster, coal handling projects, a roaster plant, stacker reclaimers/wagon tipplers, and a hybrid tandem wagon tippler.

nodes.title: Significant Initiatives
nodes.summary:

à First robotic welding machine for crusher rotors successfully installed at Kansbahal Works, which will enhance weld quality and reduce welding man-hours by 75% thereby ensuring safer operations à Kansbahal Works is certified ISO 3834-2:2021 and EN 1090-2:2008

nodes.title: Outlook
nodes.summary: The text describes Asia's dominance in steel production, with India emerging as a major beneficiary as Japan and South Korea decline. India is on track to meet 2030 targets, supported by mining privatisation, investments in beneficiation and pelletisation, and capacity expansions. The non-ferrous sector, especially aluminium and zinc, is expanding, and the Middle East is becoming an attractive investment destination due to low energy costs, investor-friendly policies, and infrastructure projects in the UAE and Oman. The overall outlook for FY 2025-26 is positive, driven by capacity expansions, technological innovations, and strategic investments in the global minerals and metals industry.

nodes.title: ENERGY PROJECTS SEGMENT
nodes.summary: The Energy Projects segment encompasses Hydrocarbon, CarbonLite Solutions, and Green & Clean Energy businesses. In FY 2024-25, order inflows rose 18.7% to ₹87,569 crore, driven by an ultra-mega Hydrocarbon order and BTG orders, with international share dropping to 60%. Revenue increased 37.6% to ₹40,689 crore due to strong Hydrocarbon execution, while Power declined. International revenue share rose to 66%, and operating margin fell to 8.4% from 10.0%. Funds employed decreased 57.1% to ₹2,482 crore. The Hydrocarbon business offers integrated turnkey solutions globally, with verticals in Offshore, Onshore EPC, Modular Fabrication, AdVENT, Asset Management, and Offshore Wind. The outlook covers oil prices, OPEC+ strategies, Middle East investments, India's refining capacity growth, offshore wind expansion, sustainability trends like CCUS, localisation policies, competition, and challenges such as labour shortage and inflation. The business secured near-record order inflows of ₹63,400 crore and revenue of ₹38,618 crore, with a positive outlook driven by strategic partnerships, digital transformation, and sustainability initiatives.

nodes.title: a) Hydrocarbon Business
nodes.summary: The Energy Projects segment covers Hydrocarbon, CarbonLite Solutions (rebranded from Energy-Power), and Green & Clean Energy businesses. Financial performance shows order inflows of ₹87,569 crore in FY 2024-25, up 18.7% year-on-year, driven by an ultra-mega Hydrocarbon order and BTG orders in CarbonLite Solutions, with international order share dropping to 60% from 87%. Revenue from operations reached ₹40,689 crore, a 37.6% increase, due to strong Hydrocarbon execution, while Power business declined from lower opening order book. International revenue share rose to 66% from 58%, and operating margin fell to 8.4% from 10.0% due to early-stage execution of new Hydrocarbon orders. Funds employed decreased 57.1% to ₹2,482 crore from reduced contract assets.

nodes.title: Overview
nodes.summary: This text provides an overview of a Hydrocarbon business, detailing its integrated 'design and build' turnkey solutions across engineering, procurement, fabrication, construction, installation, and project management. It covers global fabrication facilities in India, the Middle East, and KSA, and describes business verticals: Offshore (EPCIC solutions and marine assets), Onshore EPC (LSTK solutions for midstream/downstream), Modular Fabrication (plants and modules up to 6,600 MT), AdVENT (engineering and technology services), Asset Management (O&M and performance enhancement), and Offshore Wind (EPCI for substations and foundations). It discusses the business environment, including energy transition, CCUS demand, and risks like currency fluctuation and geopolitical tensions. Major achievements include orders from Qatar Energy LNG, ONGC, and RCF, and completed projects like decommissioning for BG Exploration and LNG tanks for Petronet. Significant initiatives in productivity, value engineering, digitalisation, and smart procurement are also highlighted.

nodes.title: Outlook
nodes.summary: The text covers the hydrocarbon sector's outlook, emphasizing oil prices and OPEC+ strategies, with KSA, UAE, and Qatar investing in offshore development. It highlights India's refining capacity growth (~68 MMTPA), natural gas share targets, and pipeline/LNG investments. Offshore wind growth (~80 GW by 2024, 28% CAGR) is noted, with Europe leading and Asian markets like India (VGF of ₹7,450 crore for 1 GW, 4 GW pipeline, ~3% global share by early 2030s). Sustainability trends include CCUS and energy-efficient designs, refinery-petrochemical integration, and decarbonisation. Middle East localisation policies (IKTVA, ICV) shape awards. Competition from European, Korean, and Chinese EPC players is intense. Challenges include labour shortage, raw material costs, and inflation, countered via procurement optimisation, automation, and Advanced Work Packaging. The business secured near-record order inflows (₹63,400 crore, down 10.6%, 82% international) and revenue of ₹38,618 crore (up 45.6%, 69% international), with operating margin declining to 8.4%. The outlook remains positive with strategic partnerships, digital transformation, and sustainability initiatives.

nodes.title: CarbonLite Solutions Business
nodes.summary: L&T Energy - CarbonLite Solutions (LTECLS), formerly L&T Energy - Power, is a leading EPC player for BTG islands of coal-based power plants, rebranded in FY 2024-25 to focus on carbon-capture, nuclear turbine islands, and pumped storage turbines while continuing domestic coal BTG solutions. It operates from Vadodara with manufacturing at Hazira (4,000 MW capacity) and has JVs with MHI, MELCO, Howden, and Sargent & Lundy. India's peak power demand hit 250 GW in FY 2024-25, with 80 GW additional coal capacity targeted by FY 2031-32; nuclear (100 GW by 2047), carbon capture, and ~20 GW pumped storage are planned. Achievements include BTG orders, commercial operations, boiler light-ups, and FGD milestones. Digital initiatives and QEHS focus are highlighted. Financials show order inflow of ₹24,153 crore (up >100%) and revenue of ₹2,059 crore (down 32.4%) with OPM at 11.9%.

nodes.title: L&T Green & Clean Energy Business
nodes.summary: The text outlines L&T's Green & Clean Energy Business, covering its overview, business model, business environment, key milestones, strategic initiatives, and outlook. It details three pillars: EPC (LTEGL) focusing on turnkey clean energy solutions including green hydrogen, ammonia, and methanol; Manufacturing (LTEL) producing indigenously developed alkaline electrolysers at a 400 MW Hazira facility; and Development spearheading large-scale green hydrogen assets via LTEGK. It discusses the business environment, including global momentum, India's National Green Hydrogen Mission, and L&T's integrated strategy. Key milestones include PLI award, FEED order, land acquisition, electrolyser dispatch, and robotic assembly line. Strategic initiatives cover technology partnerships, global collaborations, capacity expansion to gigawatt-level, and R&D. Outlook emphasizes cost competitiveness, bankable offtake contracts, policy advocacy, and scalable manufacturing for domestic and global demand.

nodes.title: HI-TECH MANUFACTURING SEGMENT
nodes.summary: The Hi-Tech Manufacturing segment comprises Heavy Engineering and Precision Engineering & Systems. Financial data shows order inflow of ₹18,282 crore in FY2024-25 (up 28.0% y-o-y), revenue of ₹10,181 crore (16.1% growth), operating margin of 17.3%, and funds employed of ₹2,250 crore. Heavy Engineering is a global leader in engineered-to-order reactors and heat exchangers for refinery, petrochemical, fertiliser, oil & gas, and nuclear sectors, with the digitally enabled A. M. Naik complex at Hazira. It is organized into product business units and has achieved key deliveries, international orders, and digital transformation. Outlook is positive, driven by renewable diesel, biodiesel, SAF, oil-to-chemicals, and LNG projects. Heavy Engineering order inflow rose 26.6% to ₹4,956 crore, with international share increasing to 76%. Precision Engineering & Systems covers nuclear, aerospace, and defence, with longstanding DRDO and Indian Navy collaborations, shipyard capabilities, land systems, space partnerships with ISRO, and production centres. It has delivered over 250 indigenous systems and has a differentiated in-house R&D model. Defence business ethics and non-proliferation commitments are noted. Market environment includes DPSU dominance shift, 2025 reforms, acquisition approvals, export/production targets, supply chain strains, and space sector opening. Major achievements include K9 Vajra repeat order, fleet support ships, light tank prototype, water jet propulsion, CMS breakthrough, ISRO's 100th mission, and RAN empanelment. R&D initiatives in armoured systems, AI, and Industry 4.0 are highlighted. Outlook covers India's FY 2025-26 Defence capital acquisition budget of ₹1,80,000 crore, with allocations for domestic industry, DRDO R&D, shipbuilding subsidies, and private-sector R&D fund. L&T's role in space subsystems and opportunities in shipbuilding, artillery, combat engineering, electronics, and space are noted. Precision Engineering & Systems reported order inflow of ₹13,326 crore (28.9% growth) and revenue of ₹6,185 crore (31.8% growth) with 15.3% margin. IT & Technology Services segment revenue was ₹48,453 crore (7.9% growth), 19.5% margin, and funds employed of ₹37,703 crore, plus an overview of LTIMindtree.

nodes.title: HI-TECH MANUFACTURING SEGMENT (intro)
nodes.summary: The Hi-Tech Manufacturing segment comprises Heavy Engineering and Precision Engineering & Systems businesses. Revenue from operations reached ₹10,181 crore, a 16.1% growth, though international revenue share fell to 22% from 29% due to tapering execution of key international jobs. Operating margin improved to 17.3% from 16.3% on execution cost savings. Funds employed increased 66.3% to ₹2,250 crore, mainly due to acquiring the remaining 26% stake in LTSSHF from NPCIL. The text also references specific projects: a screw plug heat exchanger for ICA Fluor Daniel, Mexico, and a molten salt bath reactor system with MCC Japan technology for IOCL, Dumad, Gujarat.

nodes.title: Overview
nodes.summary: The text provides an overview of the Heavy Engineering business, a global leader in engineered-to-order reactors and heat exchangers for refinery, petrochemical, fertiliser, oil & gas, and nuclear sectors. It highlights the A. M. Naik complex at Hazira, a digitally enabled manufacturing complex with in-house engineering and skilled teams. The business is organized into product business units (PBUs): Reactor & Pressure Vessels, Heat Transfer Equipment, Process Plant Internals, Modification, Revamp & Upgrade, Nuclear, Special Fabrication Unit, and L&T Special Steels & Heavy Forgings. It covers the business environment, noting geopolitical challenges but domestic market strength, and new nuclear policy initiatives aiming for 100 GW by 2047. Major achievements include delivering critical equipment, winning international orders (e.g., Woodside LNG, Marathon, Imperial Oil, Ceyhan), domestic successes (17th urea reactor, NPCIL steam generators), and significant digital transformation initiatives (iRUDRA).

nodes.title: Outlook
nodes.summary: The text outlines a positive business outlook driven by renewable diesel, biodiesel, sustainable aviation fuel, oil-to-chemicals in Asia, and LNG projects in the USA and Middle East. The MRU business is a reliable brownfield contractor in India and GCC, with growth from opex spending, oil-to-chemicals, gas-to-chemicals, coal gasification, fertiliser plant revamps, and energy efficiency projects. Heavy Engineering order inflow rose 26.6% to ₹4,956 crore, with international share increasing from 57% to 76% due to a nuclear equipment order. Revenue remained steady at ₹4,044 crore, with international share decreasing from 49% to 45%. Operating margin improved from 17.7% to 21.6% due to execution cost savings. Precision Engineering and Systems Business is mentioned.

It details longstanding DRDO and Indian Navy collaborations, shipyard capabilities, and land systems design-to-delivery solutions including artillery and armoured platforms. Space sector partnership with ISRO covers launch vehicle manufacturing, hardware, and ground facilities. The business structure spans marine, land, aerospace, and electronics, with expansion into industrial electronics. It lists production centres (Hazira, Kattupalli, Talegaon, Coimbatore, Bengaluru), over 250 indigenous systems delivered, and a differentiated in-house R&D model. Defence business ethics, non-proliferation commitments, and human rights are noted. Market environment covers DPSU dominance shift, 2025 reforms, acquisition approvals, export/production targets, supply chain strains, and space sector opening. Major achievements include K9 Vajra repeat order, fleet support ships, light tank prototype, water jet propulsion, CMS breakthrough, ISRO's 100th mission, and RAN empanelment. R&D initiatives in armoured systems, AI, and Industry 4.0 are highlighted.

nodes.title: Outlook
nodes.summary: The text covers India's FY 2025-26 Defence capital acquisition budget of ₹1,80,000 crore (up ~4.5% y-o-y), with ₹1,49,000 crore for modernisation and ₹31,000 crore for R&D and infrastructure. It details allocations: ₹1,12,000 crore for domestic industry (25% for private), ₹15,000 crore for DRDO R&D, ₹18,000 crore for SBFAP 2.0 shipbuilding subsidies, and ₹20,000 crore for a DST private-sector R&D fund. It highlights L&T's role in space subsystems and opportunities in shipbuilding, artillery, combat engineering, electronics, and space. It then reports Precision Engineering & Systems' order inflow of ₹13,326 crore (28.9% growth) and revenue of ₹6,185 crore (31.8% growth) with 15.3% margin. Finally, it covers the IT & Technology Services segment's revenue of ₹48,453 crore (7.9% growth), 19.5% margin, and funds employed of ₹37,703 crore, plus an overview of LTIMindtree.

nodes.title: IT & TECHNOLOGY SERVICES SEGMENT
nodes.summary: The text covers the IT & Technology Services segment, comprising LTIMindtree, L&T Technology Services, L&T Semiconductor Technologies, and e-commerce/digital platforms and data centers. It details the segment's financial performance for FY2024-25, including revenue growth of 7.9% to ₹48,453 crore, operating margin decline to 19.5%, and increased funds employed. A major portion focuses on LTIMindtree: its overview, business verticals (e.g., travel, healthcare, BFSI, hi-tech), service lines, alliances, business environment, key deals won, significant initiatives, and outlook. Finally, it introduces L&T Technology Services, covering its overview, global presence, and three key segments: Mobility, Sustainability, and Tech.

nodes.title: L&T Technology Services
nodes.summary: L&T Technology Services (LTTS) is a global ER&D leader with over 24,250 employees and $1.25B revenue, operating in 25+ countries. It provides design, development, and testing across product lifecycles, specializing in digital engineering, embedded systems, and analytics. LTTS serves three segments: Mobility (transportation innovation), Sustainability (discrete, industrial, process manufacturing with AI, GenAI, cybersecurity, IoT), and Tech. The section covers sustainability initiatives including a Centre of Excellence, EPCM programme, tech projects, analyst recognitions, patents, partnerships (NVIDIA, Airbus, IIT Hyderabad, Siemens), and risk management. Outlook highlights growth through 'Go Deeper to Scale' strategy, Agentic AI, mobility, sustainability, tech, the Intelliswift acquisition creating a Software & Platforms segment, and L&T Semiconductor Technologies (fabless semiconductor subsidiary with four business units).

nodes.title: Overview
nodes.summary: The text provides an overview of L&T Technology Services (LTTS), a global ER&D services leader operating in over 25 countries with annual revenue over USD 1.25 billion. It details LTTS's capabilities in design, development, and delivery of transformative products, partnering with leading brands for operational efficiency in mobility, sustainability, and tech. Headquartered in India, LTTS has over 24,250 employees, 23 global design centres, 30 sales offices, and 108 innovation labs as of March 31, 2025. The company offers end-to-end consultancy, design, development, and testing across product and process lifecycles, leveraging expertise in software and digital engineering, embedded systems, engineering analytics, and plant engineering. LTTS serves customers across three segments: Mobility, Sustainability, and Tech. The Mobility segment focuses on innovation in transportation, including automotive, aerospace, rail, and trucks/off-highway vehicles, delivering products to improve safety and consumer experiences. The text also includes image captions for LTTS offices in Bangalore and Vadodara and references the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.

nodes.title: Sustainability
nodes.summary: The text covers LTTS's sustainability-driven engineering expertise across discrete, industrial, and process manufacturing using IT-OT synergies and cross-domain insights. It details technology focus on AI (190+ patents), GenAI, cybersecurity, and connected devices for hi-tech, medtech, smart cities, and software platforms. It discusses the business environment: 9% ER&D CAGR to 2030, SDx, telecom, semiconductors, EVs (25-30% market by 2030), digital twins, IoT, and automation, alongside challenges like cost pressures, geopolitics, regulations, and competition. It highlights achievements under 'Go Deeper to Scale,' including an $80M sustainability deal, multiple $50-80M, $30-50M, and $15-25M wins, and key mobility deals with European automotive, US equipment, and automotive engineering clients.

nodes.title: Sustainability
nodes.summary: The text covers LTTS's sustainability and innovation initiatives, including a dedicated Centre of Excellence in India for digital transformation and PLM, and a major EPCM programme with an energy company. It details tech projects in healthcare, oilfield services, and telecommunications, alongside competitive positioning highlights from FY 2024-25. Analyst recognitions from Everest Group, HFS, and Zinnov are noted, as are patent filings and AI advancements like the NVIDIA AI Experience Zone. Significant initiatives include TECHgium®, Airbus CoE, partnerships with IIT Hyderabad, PST, Altair, and Siemens, and a Cyber Command Centre. The risk management framework, covering strategic, operational, financial, and compliance risks, is also summarized.

nodes.title: Outlook
nodes.summary: The text covers LTTS's outlook for robust growth through engineering and digital innovation, focusing on Agentic AI, mobility, sustainability, and tech via its 'Go Deeper to Scale' strategy. It highlights the Intelliswift acquisition expanding software and digital engineering capabilities into hyperscaler, retail, fintech, and healthcare sectors, creating a new Software & Platforms segment. It also details L&T Semiconductor Technologies (LTSCT), a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated in November 2023, aiming to be India's first fabless semiconductor product company. LTSCT has 350+ professionals globally, focuses on decarbonisation, digitalisation, and technological self-reliance, and is organized into four business units: Mobility, Industrial, Energy, and Application Solutions, each addressing specific applications and product roadmaps.

nodes.title: L&T Semiconductor Technologies
nodes.summary: The text covers L&T Semiconductor Technologies (LTSCT), a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated in November 2023, aiming to be India's first fabless semiconductor product company. It details LTSCT's global team of 350+ professionals, presence in the US, Europe, Japan, India, and Taiwan, and focus on decarbonisation, digitalisation, and technological self-reliance. The company is organized into four business units: Mobility, Industrial, Energy, and Application Solutions. The text discusses the business environment, including global and Indian semiconductor market growth, and the automotive, energy, and industrial sectors. It highlights LTSCT's products, major achievements such as product development agreements, acquisition of SiliConch Systems, establishment of a Bengaluru lab, and strategic partnerships with IBM, CDAC, and IIT Gandhinagar. Finally, it presents an outlook on geopolitical impacts and India's opportunity in the semiconductor supply chain.

nodes.title: E-commerce / Digital Platforms and Data Centers
nodes.summary: The text describes L&T's E-commerce/Digital Platforms and Data Centers sub-segment, including L&T EduTech, L&T-SuFin, and Data Centers, which leverage digital technologies for future growth. It focuses on L&T EduTech, an EdTech initiative providing hybrid education and skill building for students and professionals. L&T EduTech partners with colleges, universities, corporations, and government agencies to bridge the academia-industry skill gap. It offers a learning management system, assessment engine, recruitment automation, and skill exchange platform, with learning programs, certifications, virtual labs, capstone projects, and instructor-led training. Its two verticals are: College Connect, which aligns with NEP 2020 to integrate multi-disciplinary programs into curricula, and Workonnect, which offers upskilling/reskilling for corporate employees with courses like .Net, Java, Data Analytics, and Cybersecurity, plus an auto-proctored assessment platform for recruitment and workforce development.

nodes.title: L&T EduTech
nodes.summary: The text covers L&T's IT & Technology Services segment, focusing on digital ventures: L&T EduTech, L&T-SuFin, and Data Centers. L&T EduTech provides hybrid education and skill-building for students and professionals, partnering with academia and industry. It details its two verticals—College Connect for curriculum integration and Workonnect for corporate upskilling—along with business environment, major achievements, and outlook for the EdTech market. L&T-SuFin is a B2B digital marketplace for industrial and construction goods, featuring product discovery, RFQ, financing, and logistics. It highlights the platform's features, growth metrics, initiatives like the Seller Suvidha App, monetization strategies, and future plans. The segment aims to leverage digital technologies for future growth.

nodes.title: L&T-SuFin
nodes.summary: The text describes L&T-SuFin, a B2B digital marketplace for industrial and construction goods launched in March 2022. It covers the platform’s purpose, product range, market opportunity, key features (product discovery, RFQ-based pricing, financing, and logistics with free transit insurance), and metrics (over 7 lakh SKUs, 51 categories, 48,000 sellers, and cumulative GMV exceeding ₹5,000 crore). It also details growth initiatives: the Seller Suvidha App for MSMEs, a centralized call center and virtual relationship managers, monetization through memberships, premium plans, and advertising, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification. Finally, it outlines FY 2025-26 goals: scaling GMV with focus on retail and institutional segments, white labeling, financing solutions, and AI-driven operational and customer experience improvements.

nodes.title: Data Center and Cloud Services Business
nodes.summary: L&T-Cloudfiniti's data center and cloud business offers colocation, public/private cloud, GPU-based AI solutions, and managed services via AI-ready, secure, energy-efficient facilities. India's market grows due to digital transformation, data localization, AI/IoT/5G, and government initiatives like Digital India and India AI Mission. Capacity is expected to exceed 1,700 MW by 2025, with green data centers and sustainability as key focuses. L&T operates 14 MW live capacity in Chennai and Navi Mumbai, with 18 MW pipeline for FY2025-26, and partners with E2E Networks for GPU cloud. Competitive positioning leverages Group infrastructure expertise, AI start-up partnerships, renewable energy, and sustainable practices. Outlook cites growth in Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, driven by data protection laws and hyperscaler investments, with increasing rack density for AI workloads.

nodes.title: FINANCIAL SERVICES SEGMENT
nodes.summary: The Financial Services Segment section covers L&T Finance Limited (LTF), a AAA-rated NBFC with a ₹95,000 crore retail loan book and 97% retailisation, detailing its business segments: Rural Business Finance (group loans and microfinance), Farmer Finance, Urban Finance (two-wheeler, housing, personal, and micro loans), and SME Finance, along with growth, challenges, strategic initiatives (tech partnerships, Project Cyclops, gold loans, KAI), and risk management (credit, market/liquidity, model, IT security). It also presents the Indian economic outlook for FY 2025-26 (consumption, tax cuts, government spending, RBI regulation, credit cycle stabilization) and the financial performance of Personal Loans (revenue, disbursements, loan book, NIM, NPAs) and Development Projects (Hyderabad Metro Rail, Nabha Power, L&T IDPL stake sale, revenue/EBITDA decline, and DBFOT concession overview).

nodes.title: Overview
nodes.summary: L&T Finance Limited (LTF), a AAA-rated NBFC, completed three decades in FY 2024-25 with 97% retailisation and a ₹95,000 crore retail loan book. The text details its business segments: Rural Business Finance (group loans and microfinance for ~1.7 crore women entrepreneurs), Farmer Finance (tractor financing), Urban Finance (two-wheeler loans, retail housing, personal loans, micro loans), and SME Finance, including growth, challenges, and strategic initiatives. It covers the business environment, major achievements like tech partnerships and Project Cyclops, significant initiatives such as gold loans and KAI, and risk management areas: credit risk, market/liquidity risk, model risk, and IT security risk.

nodes.title: Outlook
nodes.summary: The text covers the Indian economic outlook for FY 2025-26, including resilient domestic consumption, Union Budget tax cuts, government spending, private expenditure, RBI regulatory approach, and credit cycle stabilization. It details the Personal Loans segment's financial performance: revenue growth, retail disbursement strategy, loan book growth, NIM decline, and NPA ratios. It also covers the Development Projects segment, comprising Hyderabad Metro Rail and Nabha Power, including the sale of L&T IDPL stake, revenue and EBITDA decline due to prior year property monetization, lower funds employed, and an overview of L&T Metro Rail (Hyderabad) Limited's DBFOT concession.

nodes.title: DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS SEGMENT
nodes.summary: The Development Projects segment covers the Hyderabad Metro Rail project via L&T Metro Rail (Hyderabad) Limited and the 2x700 MW thermal power plant through Nabha Power Limited, and reports the sale of stake in L&T Infrastructure Development Projects Limited, with segment revenue of ₹5,372 crore (down 4.5%) and operating profit of ₹1,070 crore for FY 2024-25, funds employed at ₹18,063 crore. For L&TMRHL, it details the DBFOT concession, ~70 km network, TOD monetization, four operational malls, daily ridership, IGBC Platinum certification, green initiatives, non-fare revenue, ticketing upgrades, last-mile connectivity, train overhauling, safety systems, and outlook including ridership growth, retail leasing, advertising, Phase-2 expansion. For NPL, it covers the 25-year PPA with PSPCL, coal and water sourcing, operational performance, achievements, and outlook including peak demand projections, FGD commissioning, biomass co-firing targets, and focus areas.

nodes.title: Overview
nodes.summary: The Development Projects segment covers the Hyderabad Metro Rail project via L&T Metro Rail (Hyderabad) Limited and a thermal power plant through Nabha Power Limited. It reports the sale of stake in L&T Infrastructure Development Projects Limited. Financial performance shows segment revenue of ₹5,372 crore (down 4.5%) and operating profit of ₹1,070 crore for FY 2024-25, with funds employed at ₹18,063 crore. For L&TMRHL, it details the DBFOT concession, ~70 km network, TOD monetization (4.74 million sq.ft. of 18.5 million sq.ft.), four operational malls, daily ridership (4,44,000 average, 5,63,000 peak), IGBC Platinum certification for all 57 stations, green initiatives (10 MWp solar, rainwater harvesting), non-fare revenue efforts (advertising, telecom, retail, EV charging), open-loop ticketing upgrade, last-mile connectivity, train overhauling, and safety systems like ATP and CBI.

nodes.title: Outlook
nodes.summary: The text outlines business outlooks across multiple sectors. It notes that back-to-office trends and workforce growth should boost metro ridership in FY 2025-26, with OTS easing travel and feeder services enhancing connectivity and revenue. Parking, feeder bays, elevators, and escalators remain priorities. For retail, attracting top retailers to four malls is key, with evolving leasing practices including revenue share agreements and minimum guarantees. Online sales require logistics infrastructure, and flexibility is needed to support retailers. Advertisement contract sales and partner selection have increased revenues. Hyderabad Metro is positioned as eco-friendly and reliable, with Phase-2 expansion expected to raise ridership. Nabha Power Limited is also mentioned.

nodes.title: Overview
nodes.summary: Nabha Power Limited operates a 2x700 MW supercritical thermal power plant in Rajpura, Punjab, selling power to PSPCL under a 25-year PPA until 2039. Fuel is sourced from Coal India subsidiaries via a 20-year FSA with 52.4 lakh MT annual contracted quantity, plus approvals for alternate coal. Water comes from the Bhakra-Nangal distributary, and O&M is handled in-house. The plant has run over 11 years with over 85% availability, reliably supplying Punjab and being the lowest-cost thermal producer. India's electricity demand rose 5% in FY 2024-25, while Punjab's rose ~11% to 8,951 MW. NPL sourced entirely domestic coal. Achievements include ~95% annual PAF (~98% during paddy season), 82% PLF vs 69% national average, 3% biomass co-firing, and zero reliance on alternate/imported coal.

nodes.title: Outlook
nodes.summary: Grid India projects peak demand of ~273 GW in the upcoming summer, with thermal plants holding record coal stocks of 54 MT. Punjab's peak demand is expected to reach ~17 GW in FY 2025-26, with NPL operating at high PLF and maintaining top merit order. NPL plans to commission FGD systems for both units in FY 2025-26, ahead of environmental deadlines, and has achieved 3% biomass co-firing for FY 2024-25, with a target of 5% for FY 2025-26. NPL's focus areas include HSE compliance, maximizing plant availability, improving part-load efficiency, FGD commissioning, fuel adequacy, and digitalization initiatives.

nodes.title: OTHERS SEGMENT
nodes.summary: The 'Others' segment covers Realty, Industrial Machinery, and Smart World & Communication. Realty revenue declined 8.0% to ₹7,816 crore due to fewer handovers, but operating margin improved to 29.2%. L&T Realty has 70 million sq.ft. potential across residential and commercial projects in major cities. Outlook cites stable mortgage rates, low inventories, and strong luxury demand. Construction Equipment & Others includes Komatsu distribution, LTCEL (divested to IBTPL), and Rubber Processing Machinery. Outlook notes infrastructure initiatives like NIP and CEV-V standards driving 5–6% market growth. Rubber machinery outlook projects global tyre industry growth to USD 256 billion in 2025 and USD 472 billion by 2035. L&T Valves leads in flow control solutions with global manufacturing and IoT-ready products; business environment sees stable crude prices and oil & gas investments, with new product developments.

nodes.title: a. Realty Business
nodes.summary: The 'Others' segment includes Realty Business; Industrial Machinery, Products and Others (Construction & Mining Equipment, Rubber Processing Machinery, Industrial Valves); and residual Smart World & Communication. Financial performance shows revenue from operations declined 8.0% to ₹7,816 crore in FY 2024-25 due to lower residential unit handovers in Realty. Operating margin improved to 29.2% from 21.2% on better Realty margins. Funds employed rose 8.6% to ₹8,663 crore due to new Realty project launches. A chart shows revenue and OPM% for Industrial Machinery & Others, Realty, and SWC across 2023-24 and 2024-25, with specific figures like ₹8,493 crore, ₹7,816 crore, and OPM% of 8.0%, 29.2%, and 21.2%.

nodes.title: Overview
nodes.summary: L&T Realty is a top Indian developer with 70 million sq.ft. potential across residential, commercial, and retail segments in major cities. The business model includes own land development, partnerships, and sale/leasing. The text details ongoing residential projects like Elara Celestia (Bengaluru), Avinya Enclave (Chennai), Island Cove (Mumbai), The Gateway (Mumbai), Elixir Reserve (Mumbai), Rejuve 360 (Mumbai), 77 Crossroads (Mumbai), Veridian @ Emerald Isle (Mumbai), West Square & West Manor (Navi Mumbai), and Evara Heights (Thane). Commercial projects include Seawoods Grand Central (Navi Mumbai), Innovation Campus Powai (Mumbai), Technology Park (Bengaluru), and L&T Innovation Campus (Chennai). It also covers other commercial developments, new growth opportunities with acquisitions, business environment trends (residential sales growth, office leasing, GCC demand), and major achievements including project launches, handovers, deliveries, and awards.

nodes.title: Outlook
nodes.summary: The text outlines India's real estate outlook for FY 2025-26. Residential growth is expected to continue due to stable mortgage rates and low inventories, with luxury and ultra-luxury segments remaining strong. Commercial real estate is expanding, attracting record capital inflows and leading QIP fund-raising, with exponential demand in data centers, industrial parks, and flex spaces. The office market is poised for growth, driven by strong interest in established metros (Bangalore, Mumbai, Delhi-NCR), the rise of strategic alternatives (Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune), and premiumisation of office spaces including green buildings and hospitality-grade amenities. L&T Realty is positioned to capitalize on these tailwinds.

nodes.title: Overview
nodes.summary: The text overviews L&T's Construction Equipment & Others (CE&O) business, covering the Construction & Mining Machinery (CMM) division (including CMB and LTCEL) and Rubber Processing Machinery (RPM) division. It details CMM's distribution of Komatsu equipment, LTCEL's manufacturing and divestment to IBTPL, RPM's global tyre machinery supply, and PDC's design support. The business environment discusses construction/mining demand drivers and challenges, and tyre machinery demand linked to auto sectors. Major achievements include Komatsu machine sales milestones, certifications, new excavator launch, and RPM's specialty machine developments. LTCEL's custom equipment for metro projects and initiatives like LNG retrofit kits and electric curing presses are highlighted.

nodes.title: Outlook
nodes.summary: The text covers the outlook for construction and mining machinery, driven by government infrastructure initiatives like the National Infrastructure Pipeline, Bharatmala, and Sagarmala, and the transition to CEV-V standards. It details the FY 2025-26 Union Budget's infrastructure investment, including allocations for roads, highways, and railways, and rural programs like Jal Jeevan Mission, PM Awas Yojana, and PM Gram Sadak Yojana, which are expected to boost demand for small- to mid-sized equipment and lead to 5–6% market growth. It also notes that infrastructure development will drive demand for mining machines and heavy earthmoving machinery due to increased coal and iron ore production targets. The Others segment focuses on capturing higher market share in spare parts and services through long-term contracts and initiatives to improve genuine spare parts sales. The rubber processing machinery business discusses the global automotive tyre industry's projected growth to USD 256 billion in 2025 and USD 472 billion by 2035, with Asia-Pacific led by India achieving 6.4% CAGR in unit growth through 2028. It mentions global tyre industry capacity utilization at around 70%, US emphasis on local manufacturing, potential cautious approach due to tariffs on tyre manufacturing machinery, steady Indian demand with focus on PCR and TBR tyres, and low OHT utilization with no significant investments anticipated in FY 2025-26. Finally, it provides an overview of L&T Valves Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of L&T, describing its leadership in flow control solutions, global customer base, manufacturing excellence, key sectors served, product range, certifications, IoT-ready digital solutions, after-market services, manufacturing facilities in Kancheepuram and Al Jubail, internal engineering and R&D, and established safety and quality record. It also covers the business environment for industrial valves in FY 2024-25, including stable crude oil prices, easing inflation, increased oil & gas investments, demand from LNG shift, challenges like shorter lead times and stringent regulations, market fragmentation, and competitive environment. Major product developments are listed: a first globe valve with Inconel 625 cladded internals, a hydraulic drain valve operated under sea and actuated from 6 metres above sea level, and exotic grade material valves for Bio Refinery and PTA plants.

nodes.title: L&T Valves Limited
key_items: World’s largest Bellow-sealed Gate Valve supplied for Benzene service in a refinery
nodes.summary: The text provides an overview of L&T Valves Limited (LTVL), a wholly owned subsidiary of L&T, detailing its global leadership in flow control solutions, key sectors served, product range (including API-monogrammed valves and IoT-ready digital solutions), certifications, and after-market services. It describes manufacturing facilities in India and Saudi Arabia, in-house engineering and R&D. The business environment section notes stable crude prices, easing inflation, and increased oil & gas investments driving valve demand, alongside challenges like shorter lead times and stringent regulations in a fragmented, competitive market. Major product developments include complex engineering products such as a globe valve with Inconel cladding, hydraulic drain valve, exotic material valves, buried service ball valve, and the world's largest bellow-sealed gate valve. The outlook monitors demand indicators, geopolitical risks, tariff impacts, and domestic opportunities in fleet projects, SMR/BSR initiatives, and thermal power, with focus on expansion, digitalisation, and operational excellence.

nodes.title: INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
nodes.summary: L&T's IT function invested in technology and infrastructure to enhance governance, efficiency, and sustainable growth. Key FY 2024-25 initiatives include digital transformation with AI solutions, compliance with ISO 27001:2022 and SEBI regulations via NARADA, cybersecurity enhancements through C-SOC and training, and sustainability via the L&T-EARTH platform. Future priorities include scaling the L&T One Approach, advancing Industry 5.0, AI innovation, ESG excellence, and cyber resilience. The Human Resources section highlights five foundational pillars for human capital development aligned with Lakshya 2026, talent acquisition of over 4,200 young professionals, employer branding through campus engagements and competitions, performance management and succession planning with Development Centres and Talent Reviews, and special worker retention initiatives.

nodes.title: HUMAN RESOURCES
nodes.summary: L&T's Human Resources section covers its people-centric approach, including talent acquisition (over 2,600 GETs/PGETs and 1,600 other professionals), employer branding, and diversity (30% women hires). It details performance management, succession planning, and talent review processes, along with special worker incentive schemes. Learning and development initiatives include leadership programs, long-term education, skilling (10,000+ via CSTI), and ATL Varsity. HR digitalization features AI tools like HEERA Plus, CAISY, and Retain Pulse.AI. DEI efforts include PwD hiring and WINSPIRE for women. Employee engagement involves Pulse surveys, podcasts, and QuizWiz. Health and well-being programs cover mental health first aid and marathons. The section concludes with outlook, strategic priorities, and awards.

nodes.title: AWARDS AND ACCOLADES
nodes.summary: The section covers L&T's extensive awards and accolades across multiple domains. It highlights the Golden Peacock Award for CSR, numerous EHS awards from RoSPA and NSCI, and HR recognitions including Great Place to Work certification, ET HR World Future Skills, Skillsoft, AVTAR, SHRM, Randstad, Forbes, and ETHCA. CSR recognitions include the India CSR Investment in Sustainability Award, AIMA's Unnati prize, and ICC's sustainability award. Business-specific awards include ICI and ACCE for Buildings & Factories, Build India Infra and EPC World for Transportation Infrastructure, IMC RBNQA and MEED for Water & Effluent Treatment, SPE, ICC OHS, and OHSSAI for Hydrocarbon, and Skoch Order of Merit for Precision Engineering & Systems. L&T Technology Services was recognized as a Great Place to Work in the US and Poland. Additionally, 2024 recognitions include Top 100 Best Companies for Women in India by AVTAR & Seramount, Zinnov leader in Digital Engineering and ER&D Services, Financial Express FuTech Awards for AR/VR and analytics, Nabha Power's CBIP, CEE, and CII awards, CEE awards for sustainable performance, SHRM HR Excellence Gold Award, Construction Equipment awards, and Valves' EEPC Star Performer Award, OHSSAI Gold, and ISO 19443:2018 certification.

Water & Effluent Treatment earned IMC RBNQA and MEED awards. Hydrocarbon received SPE, ICC OHS, and OHSSAI carbon neutrality awards. structure.summary: The Integrated Report section covers L&T's sustainability disclosures, including reporting frameworks (IIRC <IR>, BRSR/NGRBC), reporting period (April 1, 2024–March 31, 2025), standalone scope, and external assurance by Deloitte for BRSR Core. It details the value creation model, six capitals (natural, manufactured, human, intellectual, social & relationship, financial), stakeholder engagement, material topics, and sustainability governance. It presents performance across natural capital (energy, emissions, water, waste, biodiversity), manufactured capital (EPC projects, manufacturing, green business), human capital (workforce, talent, learning, safety, DEI), intellectual capital (R&D, digital transformation, innovation), social & relationship capital (CSR, community development, supply chain), and financial capital (order inflow, revenue, economic value distribution). It also includes climate scenario analysis, risks/opportunities, outlook, and BRSR disclosures.

nodes.title: Integrated Report (intro)
nodes.summary: This Integrated Annual Report section outlines the approach to sustainability disclosures, covering value creation for stakeholders, a sustainability performance overview, value creation model, sustainability governance, material topics, stakeholder engagement, and the six capitals. It details reporting frameworks (IIRC <IR> Framework and BRSR based on NGRBC), reporting period (April 1, 2024–March 31, 2025) on a standalone basis, and external assurance by Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP for BRSR Core parameters.
