nodes.title: VALUE CREATION MODEL
nodes.summary: This value creation model outlines six capitals: natural (water, energy, environmental spend, materials), manufactured (project sites, facilities), human (employees, workers, diversity, safety training), intellectual (R&D spend, IPR, engineers, collaborations), social (CSR spend, partners, MSME sourcing, industry memberships), and financial (order book, assets). It details business processes and the L&T Business Excellence Model, including value engineering, lean operations, and integrated engineering. It lists key infrastructure and facility types. Multiple footnotes explain environmental spend, partnerships, green building, mobility infrastructure, and irrigation. The document is part of an Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.

nodes.title: Offerings
nodes.summary: The text outlines offerings across speed & scale (commercial spaces, airports, solar and nuclear power plants, refining/petchem, ferrous/non-ferrous plants, launch vehicles) and digitalisation, automation, innovation, global sourcing. It reports SDG linkage metrics: GHG emissions 0.88 Mn tCO2e, emission intensity 6.2 tCO2e/₹Cr, water offset 3.2 Mn kL/year, green business revenue ~₹75,500 Cr. Infrastructure created includes building 30.7 Mn sq. ft., mobility 921, bridges/tunnels 50.2 km, transmission lines 2,304 ckm, solar 4.3 GWp, water storage 529 Mn ltr and treatment 910 Mn ltr/day, factory output 3,34,304 tonnes. HR metrics: revenue per employee ₹2.4 Cr, 112 women in senior management, 10.1 training days, 1,380 Mn accident-free man hours, 3 IPR grants, 313 value engineering projects, 1.9 Mn CSR beneficiaries, ₹7,481 Cr exchequer contribution, 1,250 complaints received and 1,181 resolved. Financials: turnover ₹1,42,509 Cr, PBIT ₹15,294 Cr, dividend ₹4,676 Cr, RoNW 15.94%, plus footnotes on value engineering, production businesses, and stakeholder complaints.

nodes.title: DRIVING STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Company's stakeholder engagement framework, emphasizing open dialogue for a resilient, sustainable business. It covers core principles like mutual value creation and inclusivity, governance by top management, and a structured engagement process (identify, prioritize, review, gather inputs, decide, communicate). It details engagement with key stakeholders: government (80% revenue, critical for infrastructure and digital transformation, with channels like review meetings and advocacy) and customers (20% revenue, long-term relationships, channels like satisfaction surveys, focus on quality, timely delivery, data privacy, and value creation through collaboration and repeat business).

nodes.title: Employees and Workers
nodes.summary: The text emphasizes the workforce as the Company's backbone, driving productivity, innovation, and culture. It outlines engagement channels like townhalls, surveys, training, appraisals, grievance processes, circulars, welfare initiatives, the HEERA AI assistant, and events. Key focus areas include continuous communication on work environment, development, health and safety, compensation, business outlook, and policies. It also covers feedback, skill development, career growth, well-being, employee satisfaction, operational efficiency, and a safe workplace. Frequency ranges from continuous to annual and need-based.

nodes.title: Supply Chain Partners
nodes.summary: The text outlines L&T's stakeholder engagement framework, focusing on supply chain partners, shareholders/investors, and communities/NGO partners. For supply chain partners, it details a vast global network, engagement methods (conferences, meetings, trainings, grievance platforms), key topics (ESG assessment, performance, compliance, risk mitigation), and value creation goals (strong relationships, ethical practices, MSME progress). For shareholders and investors, it covers their role in providing capital and influencing governance, engagement channels (investor meets, reports, AGM, digital platforms), frequency, and focus areas (performance, concerns, growth plans, trust, value enhancement). For communities and NGO partners, it describes their role in trust-building and shared value, engagement methods (direct/through NGOs, CSR projects, assessments), frequency, and focus areas (community development, local employment, infrastructure, social license, risk reduction).

nodes.title: Shareholders and Investors
nodes.summary: The text outlines L&T's engagement with shareholders and investors, emphasizing their role in providing capital, influencing governance through voting rights, and aligning with value creation and transparency. It lists engagement channels such as investor meets, annual reports, AGM, quarterly results, investor relations, website, social media, one-on-one meetings, regulatory filings, newsletters, press releases, stock exchange filings, and dedicated contact methods. Engagement frequency includes AGM and quarterly investor meets, with key discussion topics covering business performance (financial and non-financial), policy concerns, growth opportunities, trust in management, and value enhancement for shareholder investments.

nodes.title: Communities and NGO Partners
nodes.summary: The text outlines communities and NGO partners as essential allies for building trust, social licence, and shared value. It describes their roles: communities provide contextual insights for respectful, inclusive business; NGOs offer expertise, credibility, and networks for sustainability, community engagement, and social development. Engagement methods include direct or NGO-facilitated interaction, CSR implementation, needs and impact assessments, community visits, meetings, and village institution formation. Frequency is need-based or quarterly with NGO partners. Key activities cover community development programs, local employment, concern resolution, infrastructure strengthening, and livelihoods. Outcomes include social licence, positive impact, improved living standards, empowerment, enhanced relations, risk reduction, conflict avoidance, and employee engagement and morale, all under value creation and stakeholder engagement.

nodes.title: Regulatory Bodies
nodes.summary: The text covers regulatory bodies and media as key stakeholders. For regulators, it details their role in shaping the business environment, L&T's engagement channels (industry associations, collaborative initiatives, direct interactions, public consultations, audits), key focus areas (compliance, governance, policy inputs, transparency, climate change), and outcomes (enhanced compliance, brand reputation, national goals contribution, sector advancement). For media, it highlights their role in public perception, engagement channels (interviews, press briefings, press releases, quarterly results, annual report, AGM, crisis communication, social media), frequency, key topics (financial results, project wins, strategic initiatives, business updates, sustainability), and outcomes (brand value, public perception, strategic input, disclosure).

nodes.title: Media
nodes.summary: The text covers stakeholder engagement with regulatory bodies and media. For regulators, it details their role in setting standards, L&T's engagement through industry associations, policy advocacy, collaborative initiatives, direct interactions, public consultations, audits, and compliance, with key focus areas including policy inputs, transparency, climate change, and corporate governance, aiming for enhanced compliance, brand reputation, and sector development. For media, it describes media's role in shaping perception, engagement channels like interviews, press releases, quarterly results, annual reports, AGM, crisis communication, and social media, with focus areas including financial results, project wins, strategic initiatives, and sustainability, aiming to enhance brand value and provide strategy input. It also includes a legend explaining frequency, engagement channels, and key focus areas.

nodes.title: OUTLOOK AND STRATEGIC PRIORITIES
nodes.summary: L&T outlines its stakeholder engagement strategy to strengthen relationships and align with strategic goals. Key areas include: enhancing communication via traditional and digital platforms; inclusive decision-making through forums and workshops; community engagement with local organizations for social development, education, skilling, healthcare, water, sanitation, and environmental conservation; regular stakeholder surveys to inform strategy; prioritizing ESG principles through double materiality and co-created sustainable solutions; and transparent reporting via sustainability reports and project updates. These efforts aim to build trust, foster cooperation, and promote sustainable, inclusive growth.

nodes.title: UNDERSTANDING MATERIALITY
nodes.summary: L&T's materiality assessment identifies significant ESG topics aligned with stakeholder expectations and business objectives, balancing stakeholder concerns with strategic importance. Conducted every three years with annual reviews, the 2022 structured assessment engaged internal and external stakeholders to identify relevant sustainability topics. L&T initiated its first double materiality exercise, evaluating topics through inside-out (company impacts on society/environment) and outside-in (sustainability issues affecting business) lenses, expected to conclude in FY 2025-26. Outcomes will enhance ESG risk/opportunity identification, transparency, and sustainability integration. The framework includes benchmarking, stakeholder prioritization, issue shortlisting, and topic finalization, with key external and internal stakeholders listed.

nodes.title: MATERIAL TOPICS
nodes.summary: The text details the material topics identification process: initially 32 potential topics were found, and 14 were finalized as most pertinent for short-, medium-, and long-term value creation from stakeholder perspectives, with ongoing monitoring and review. It then lists these 14 topics, not ranked, categorized into Environment (Climate Action; Water, Waste and Hazardous Materials Management), Social (Employee and Workforce Engagement, Well-Being, Health and Safety; Human Rights and Labour Conditions; Skilled Manpower; Talent Management – Attraction, Retention and Development; Diversity, Inclusion and Equal Opportunity; Social Engagement and Impact), Economic (Customer Experience and Satisfaction; Quality of Products and Project Delivery; Sustainable Supply Chain), and Governance (Business Ethics; Brand Management; Data Security, Privacy and Cybersecurity).

nodes.title: Overview of the Material Topics
nodes.summary: The text outlines material topics for L&T, covering climate action (risks/opportunities, carbon/water neutrality targets, risk integration); water, waste, and hazardous materials management (compliance, recycling, sustainable sourcing); employee engagement, well-being, health and safety (ISO 45001, training, well-being); human rights and labour conditions (supplier code, grievance mechanisms, due diligence); skilled manpower (training, sourcing, retention); talent management (attraction, retention, development); diversity, inclusion and equal opportunity; social engagement and impact; customer experience and satisfaction; quality of products and project delivery; business ethics (code of conduct, whistleblower policy); brand management; data security, privacy and cybersecurity (ISO 27001, security operations); and sustainable supply chain (supplier code, ESG assessments). Each topic includes why it is material and approaches to adapt or mitigate risks, with capital classifications and financial implications.

nodes.title: SUSTAINABILITY GOVERNANCE AND MANAGEMENT
nodes.summary: The text covers L&T's sustainability governance and management, emphasizing the integration of ESG principles into decision-making for long-term stakeholder value. It details the strategy under Lakshya 2026 and the upcoming Lakshya 2031, including redefined social obligations and sustainability goals. A multi-tiered governance structure is described: Board oversight via the CSR & Sustainability Committee (with specific terms of reference), executive leadership through the Executive Committee, and various councils and committees (e.g., Group CSR Council, HRC Council, EHS Council, Green Campus Task Force, Material Council, IT & Cybersecurity Council, Quality Council) with their scopes and heads. Corporate Sustainability and business-level teams are also outlined, with the Chief Sustainability Officer leading policy formulation and performance monitoring.

nodes.title: COUNCILS AND SCOPE COMMITTEES
nodes.summary: This text outlines corporate governance and sustainability structures, covering an overview, management discussion, integrated report, statutory reports, and financial statements. It details councils and committees, including the Group CSR Council and its members, and categorizes councils by capital: Manufactured Capital (Green Campus/Sustainability Task Force), Human Capital (HRC Council), Intellectual Capital (EHS, Material, IT & Cybersecurity, Quality Councils), each with focus areas and leaders. It also describes corporate sustainability governance at corporate and business levels, including a Chief Sustainability Officer-led team and business-level representatives, and references sustainability governance, strategy, corporate tasks, and operational responsibility.

nodes.title: CSR & SUSTAINABILITY COMMITTEE
nodes.summary: The text outlines the CSR & Sustainability Committee's governance structure, including Executive, Corporate Sustainability, and Business-level committees with functional and unit-level teams. It details sustainability policies (Sustainability, Code of Conduct, Sustainable Supply Chain, EHS, Equal Opportunity, Anti-Bribery) and reporting standards (Integrated Annual Report, BRSR, CDP, ESG ratings). Key initiatives include decarbonisation, water neutrality, employee training, stakeholder engagement, sustainable supply chain, and waste reduction. It describes management systems (ISO 9001, 14001, 45001, etc.) and certifications. The Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption section covers governance, policy applicability, key components (zero tolerance, due diligence, monitoring), training, and performance (zero fines, 77% training completion).

nodes.title: Approach to Business Ethics
nodes.summary: The text outlines the company's business ethics approach, including governance and ethical leadership with codes of conduct, ethics training, and whistleblower protection mechanisms for employees and vendors. It details the whistleblower policy features: confidentiality, non-retaliation, reporting channels, investigation process, and accountability. An external ethics audit reviewed policies and led to improvements in anti-bribery, due diligence, code of conduct, whistleblower procedures, and training. The POSH policy ensures a harassment-free workplace with zero tolerance, apex committees, ICCs, reporting channels, confidential investigations, retaliation protection, and awareness sessions. Cybersecurity governance covers board oversight, regulatory compliance, risk identification, multi-layered defense, crisis management, data privacy, training, vendor risk management, and standards certification. Reasonable assurance on BRSR Core KPIs by an independent third party ensures ESG data credibility. The company's commitment to corporate governance and sustainability is highlighted.

nodes.title: SUSTAINABILITY HIGHLIGHTS OF FY 2024-25
nodes.summary: This sustainability highlights report for FY 2024-25 begins with the company's materiality assessment, which identified 14 ESG material topics, selecting at least one KPI per topic. Environmental metrics cover energy, emissions, and water consumption intensities, recycled materials, green business revenue (with improvement noted), renewable electricity, and saplings planted. Social metrics include safety training hours, human rights certification and training, workforce skilling, gender diversity and women in senior management, and CSR beneficiaries. Governance metrics encompass Code of Conduct training, brand management with ESG ratings (climate change and environmental rankings), customer satisfaction, data privacy breaches, and sustainable supply chain partner assessments and green ratings.

nodes.title: SOCIAL
nodes.summary: The text covers corporate social, governance, and natural capital aspects. Social points include health and safety training hours, human rights certifications and training, workforce skilling, diversity metrics, and CSR beneficiaries. Governance points cover ethics training, customer satisfaction, ESG ratings, data privacy, sustainable supply chain assessments, and environmental firm ranking. Natural capital section discusses environmental stewardship, dependencies on land use and ecosystems, and integration into environmental management strategy and long-term vision.

nodes.title: NATURAL CAPITAL

nodes.title: Carbon Neutrality Strategy
nodes.summary: The Company targets carbon neutrality (Scope 1 & 2) by 2040, using FY 2020-21 baseline emissions intensity and business growth assumptions for BAU projections. The roadmap is phased into short-term (1-2 years), medium-term (2-5 years), and long-term (5-15 years) horizons aligned with its 5-year plan Lakshya. Diesel contributes over 75% of energy consumption and electricity around 17%, driving carbon footprint. GHG emissions are expected to peak around FY 2025-26 then decline. Key levers include reducing energy intensity via operational efficiency, process optimization, and conservation in the medium term, and transitioning to renewable electricity and low/zero-carbon fuels in the long term. The decarbonization path involves optimizing equipment utilization, controlling losses, deploying energy-efficient and electric machinery, switching to renewable electricity and low-carbon fuels, and carbon sequestration through plantation, with emission reductions from energy efficiency (~35%), decarbonizing energy use (~55%), and offsets (~10%).

nodes.title: Reducing Energy Intensity
nodes.summary:
Reducing Energy Intensity
Diesel is the Company’s major energy source. Cutting down on diesel consumption helps reduce both energy intensity and GHG emissions. The Company formed a task force in FY 2023-24 to explore and implement solutions to reduce diesel consumption across the business units of the Company.
Key solutions being implemented are:
Switching from Diesel Generator (DG) sets to grid electricity supply
Replacing fuel-powered older equipment with more energy-efficient ones
Replacing diesel-powered equipment with electricity-powered ones
Switching to use of hybrid or electric equipment, e.g. light masts, wheel loaders
In addition, the business units are replacing older equipment with more energy-efficient ones to reduce the consumption of electricity, e.g. Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) or Variable Voltage Variable Frequency (VVFD) to replace conventional drives, 5-star rated appliances to replace 3-star ones, auto control of lighting, and so on.

nodes.title: Decarbonising Energy Consumption
nodes.summary: The Company is decarbonising energy consumption by increasing renewable electricity sourcing through a task force exploring Power Purchase Agreements (solar, wind, hybrid), on-site solar installation (capex/opex), green tariffs, and open access via developers, third-parties, and group captive. It also blends biodiesel with diesel to reduce fossil fuel reliance in stationary and mobile combustion. Business units are transitioning to low- and zero-carbon fuels like CNG, CBG, and biomass pellets. These initiatives lower the carbon footprint, enhance energy diversification and resilience, with solar installations at Talegaon and Kansbahal facilities noted under Natural Capital.

nodes.title: Redesigned Zero Liquid Discharge to improve Water Recovery
nodes.summary:
Redesigned Zero Liquid Discharge to improve Water Recovery
Industries across sectors are increasingly challenged by water scarcity and wastewater pollution. Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems offer a sustainable solution by recycling wastewater and eliminating liquid discharge. However, conventional ZLD processes are resource-intensive, requiring substantial steam, power and cooling water, which can limit their efficiency and scalability.
Accordingly, the Water and Effluent Treatment business developed an innovative ZLD system for IOCL Vadodara Refinery. The redesigned process treats wastewater from the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) and cooling tower blowdown using a sequence of pre-treatment, ultrafiltration, reverse osmosis (RO) and ion exchange to produce high-quality demineralised water.

While ensuring the safe and compliant disposal of waste is critical to minimising environmental and community impacts, the Company emphasises maximising reuse and recycling of materials. This approach reduces dependency on virgin natural resources. Also, it helps lower emissions associated with transporting waste to external disposal sites and diverting waste from landfilling.
A significant portion of non-hazardous waste is generated at the Company’s EPC project sites. In alignment with the circular economy principles, the locations are encouraged to identify and implement on-site reuse and recycling solutions to minimise off-site disposal.

nodes.title: EPC Projects
nodes.summary: The text outlines EPC Projects, covering businesses with end-to-end design-to-deliver capabilities in infrastructure, energy, and metals. It details sectors: Buildings & Factories (tech-enabled solutions for various building types), Transportation Infrastructure (turnkey design and build for roads, bridges, railways, airports), Heavy Civil Infrastructure (large civil works like high-speed rail, nuclear plants, tunnels, ports), Power Transmission & Distribution (technology-focused solutions), Water & Effluent Treatment (EPC for treatment and distribution), Renewables (solar PV, storage, microgrids), Minerals & Metals (EPC from processing to finished metals), L&T Energy - Hydrocarbon (integrated solutions for oil & gas), and L&T Energy - CarbonLite Solutions (gas-to-power, carbon capture, low-carbon power plants). It also includes report references and page numbers.

nodes.title: Hi-Tech Manufacturing
key_items: A. M. Naik Heavy Engineering Complex, Hazira, Gujarat
nodes.summary: The text details Hi-Tech Manufacturing's globally recognised facilities for engineered-to-order equipment across process plants, nuclear power, aerospace, oil & gas, and other sectors. It describes specific complexes: A. M. Naik Heavy Engineering Complex (Hazira) for ultra-heavy equipment and modular fabrication; Strategic Systems Complex (Talegaon) for precision engineering, sensors, and electronics; Modular Fabrication Facility (Kattupalli) for offshore/onshore modules and offshore wind; multiple units in Kancheepuram for transmission towers, engineered systems for core industries, and tyre/rubber machinery, plus a Transmission Tower Testing and Research Station; and a Shipbuilding Facility (Kattupalli) for ship construction and repair. Other units are in Pithampur, Kansbahal, Ranoli, and Coimbatore. It references the Management Discussion and Analysis section for further details on capabilities, achievements, and sector outlook.

nodes.title: Green Business
nodes.summary: L&T's Green Business is a core strategic priority driven by two objectives: harnessing Energy Transition opportunities (SO-III) and enabling long-term sustainability via ESG principles and shareholder value (SO-V). The portfolio addresses clean energy, mobility, water and sanitation, green infrastructure, and emerging domains, helping customers achieve energy efficiency, emissions reduction, water efficiency, wastewater recycling, pollutant reduction, and resource conservation. Revenues are classified using FTSE GRCS 2.0, aligned with EU Taxonomy. Green Business constituted 53% (~₹75,500 crore) of FY 2024-25 revenue (up from 50% in FY 2023-24), with a revised target of 55% by FY 2025-26. L&T ranked third globally in ENR's Top 200 Environment Firms for 2022-2024. Offerings are mapped to climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies, with detailed portfolio categories and revenue shares. The text also begins a Human Capital section, recognizing employees as vital enablers of sustainable value creation.

nodes.title: L&T’s People: Enablers of Innovation and Sustainable Value Creation
nodes.summary: The text describes L&T's approach to human capital as a driver of long-term value and resilience. It emphasizes fostering a safe, inclusive, empowering work environment with prioritized well-being and continuous learning. The human capital management strategy integrates ESG considerations and is built on five pillars: fairness and inclusiveness, well-being as a strategic enabler, continuous learning and innovation culture, performance with purpose, and capability building at scale. These pillars align with the Lakshya 2026 strategy plan to ensure human capital development supports business success and stakeholder value creation. The text also includes document metadata: page number 216, Integrated Annual Report 2024-25, and section headings Corporate Overview, Management Discussion and Analysis, Integrated Report, Statutory Reports, and Financial Statements.

nodes.title: Workforce Profile and Composition
nodes.summary: The text covers L&T's workforce profile: 58,556 employees described as real assets, with a young, innovative, agile, and digitally savvy workforce from every Indian state/UT and multiple nationalities, creating a multicultural and inclusive environment. It includes age and gender distribution for total employees (under 30: 3,209 female, 18,126 male; 30-50: 1,572 female, 30,079 male; over 50: 191 female, 5,379 male; totals: 5,570 female, 31,651 male; overall 21,335 under 30, 31,651 30-50, 5,570 over 50) and for new joiners (under 30: 994 female, 4,853 male; 30-50: 197 female, 3,813 male; over 50: 6 female, 271 male; totals: 1,197 female, 8,937 male; overall 5,847 under 30, 4,010 30-50, 277 over 50). It notes nearly 5,000 women employees in critical leadership roles across engineering, construction, high-tech manufacturing, and new-age services due to gender diversity efforts.

nodes.title: Talent Acquisition and Employer Brand
nodes.summary: In FY 2024-25, the young professional talent acquisition team recruited over 2,600 engineering graduates as GETs and PGETs through campus recruitment, plus over 1,600 other young professionals including MBA graduates, chartered accountants, cost accountants, and diploma engineers. Selected GETs and PGETs undergo the GRACE induction program featuring online and offline gamified pre-joining exercises on a micro-learning platform. Employer branding efforts include targeted campus engagements, strategic sponsorships, social media campaigns, leadership talks, and industry-academia collaborations to reinforce the company's position as an employer of choice. CreaTech, a flagship case competition, offers real-world problem-solving experiences. OutThink, a new business case competition, received over 6,500 registrations from 34 B-schools, with top teams presenting to a jury. Additionally, 30% of GETs and PGETs hired over the last three years were women.

nodes.title: Talent Management
nodes.summary: The text covers talent management, including talent identification via a Performance Management System that differentiates, recognizes, and rewards talent, integrated with career development and succession planning. High-potential employees are nurtured through Development Centres and the Technology Leadership Programme, with over 1,500 employees assessed in FY 2024-25 and Individual Development Plans created. The Talent Council, comprising business and HR heads and senior executives, identifies and develops future leaders through personalized plans, cross-functional projects, training, leadership shadowing, and coaching, supported by a digital tool. The Talent Review Process is strengthened with quality discussions and a software module. The FAIR Process performance management system rewards excellence through performance planning, SMART goal setting, cascading goals, continuous review, feedback, coaching, and fair assessment, fostering a high-performance culture based on meritocracy, entrepreneurship, teamwork, and continuous learning.

nodes.title: ESG Linkage to Performance and KPIs
nodes.summary: The text details how the Company integrates ESG metrics—such as energy and water intensity, GHG emissions, diesel reduction, renewable energy, safety, diversity and inclusion, community engagement, and compliance—into business/project-level performance indicators and individual KRAs. Business indicators are reviewed quarterly, individual KRAs twice a year, and KRAs link to annual appraisals. It also introduces a Reward and Penalty System for EPC projects, with fixed monetary rewards for units exceeding safety targets and penalties for those falling short, impacting annual performance-linked rewards or bonuses for all employees in affected units. This aligns ESG KPIs with operational excellence and financial metrics to drive measurable outcomes, risk mitigation, innovation, and long-term stakeholder returns.

nodes.title: Learning and Leadership Development
nodes.summary: The text outlines L&T's Learning and Leadership Development framework, covering a future-ready talent pool and four leadership archetypes: Business, People, Project, and Technical. It details physical and digital L&D infrastructure, the LAKSHYA Plan, Competency Framework, and L&T Business Excellence Model. Key programs include Pragati (4-step PLDP), Seven-Step Leadership Pipeline, ASCENT competency development with its six-month blended structure, Women Leadership WINSPIRE, SCDM, case centre, PM conclave, Knowledge@work, Professor of Practice, Management Development Programmes (with IIM-C, IIM-B, XLRI for 800+ employees annually), and Executive/Supervisory Development Programmes (with SIBM, NMIMS). Technical development includes Young Talent Development, Prayag fresher training, Level 1-3 Technical Development, CADFest, BIM, Safety, Railway Competency, Tunneling, Construction Vocational Training, Virtual Technical Summit, and Technology Conclave. It also mentions sustainability topics, rural immersion, coaching, simulations, and action projects.

nodes.title: L&T Leadership Development Framework and Programmes
key_items: L&T’s leadership development framework is structured around four key archetypes:
nodes.summary: L&T’s leadership development framework is built on four archetypes: Business, People, Project, and Technical Leadership. The Seven-Step Leadership Pipeline Programme, run with top business and foreign institutions, develops visionary leaders for strategic roles through seamless transitions, critical competencies, and global perspectives. New elements include sustainability topics, rural immersion, personalised coaching, simulation-based learning, and immersive projects to build socially responsible leaders. The ASCENT series, a six-month multi-level programme with top business schools, blends experiential learning, action projects, real-world challenges, simulations, and mentorship to equip leaders at all levels with strategic thinking, agility, and competencies for long-term success and smooth leadership transitions.

nodes.title: Ascent Series programme constuct

It describes Management Development Programmes (MDPs) with premier B-schools enhancing functional skills for over 800 employees annually via classroom learning, case studies, guest lectures, and curated readings, plus Executive and Supervisory Development Programmes (EDP/SDP) with SIBM and NMIMS for foundational leadership. It introduces the People Leadership Excellence Framework (FY 2023–24) covering five dimensions—Personal, Relationship, Performance, Development, and Leadership—with specific competencies, and the My People Leadership Insights tool using multi-rater feedback and AI for actionable insights. nodes.title: L&T Human Capital: Skills, Education Programmes and ATLVarsity
nodes.summary: The page covers L&T's human capital development. It highlights specialised certification programmes: the Bridge Engineering Certification with IIT Madras certifying 15 engineers, and the Tunnel Engineering Level 2 Certification with VNIT Nagpur completed by 42 employees across two batches. Long-term education programmes include the Build India Scholarship (M.Tech at IIT Madras, IIT Delhi, NIT Trichy, NIT Surathkal), Integrated Learning Programmes (B.Tech via BITS Pilani, KIIT, Nirma, LPU, VIT; M.Tech via DIAT Pune; Industrial Safety Certification via SBTET Andhra Pradesh), Project Management Education (Executive MBA with NICMAR), new co-branded M.Tech programmes with NICMAR, and MBA-equivalent programmes with IIM Ahmedabad, SPJIMR and IFMR Krea. Launched in FY 2024-25 under ATLVarsity, the People Leadership Academy uses a five-stage framework and Coursera's AI Course Builder to offer structured, business-aligned development for emerging and experienced leaders. The Engineering Academy engages technical experts, providing support and motivation. In its inaugural year, it conducted 10 specialized training programmes for 293 participants in domains like welding, structural steel design, construction safety, concrete technology, sustainable design, and formwork. It also trained 85 PGETs from premier institutions in core subjects such as building materials, structural codes, geotechnical engineering, and concrete/steel design, and inducted 87 specialized staff through expert development programmes.

nodes.title: ESG Training and Awareness Building
nodes.summary: The text details ESG training and awareness initiatives, including an ESG module in Management Development Programmes, numerous sessions by the Corporate Sustainability team and business-level coordinators covering sustainability fundamentals, data management, climate change, water security, biodiversity, human rights, diversity and inclusion, reporting compliance, and BRSR. It highlights over 60,000 hours of ESG trainings by businesses, the annual two-day ECOPHORIA conference with 130+ participants, and the goal of fostering a sustainability culture.

nodes.title: HR Digitalisation and AI Enablement
nodes.summary: L&T's HR digital transformation began in 2019 with SAP SuccessFactors. In FY 2024-25, the company launched the SuccessFactors Learning Management System for personalized, flexible, device-agnostic learning. HEERA Plus.AI, an AI-enabled chatbot, was introduced for HR query resolution, handling over 300 scenarios with contextual, real-time responses using Generative AI. CAISY, a Conversational AI Simulator, offers over 70 scenarios for manager coaching across three personas. A digital library via Percipio provides access to over 15,000 books and articles. An AI-based 270-degree report in the People Leadership Excellence Feedback Instrument gives managers a comprehensive overview of competencies, strengths, and blind spots, aiding customized development plans.

nodes.title: Diversity, Equity and Inclusion
nodes.summary: L&T's DEI strategy, anchored in its four-pillar charter, includes diverse hiring (campus, RENEW for women, differently abled), DEI Academy learning journeys, Allyship Awards, and the WINSPIRE leadership series for women. The company expanded its online compensation platform and shifted to a role-based organization with a skills inventory. It supports working mothers through flexible policies and promotes women in leadership. The text also covers an all-women factory team for noise barriers on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail project, addressing gender diversity at sites, and includes employee testimonials on WINSPIRE's transformative impact.

nodes.title: Employee Experience and Engagement
nodes.summary: L&T enhances employee experience through pre-joining GRACE, Pulse Engage onboarding surveys via HEERA, and L&T Radio podcasts on leadership and wellness. The Let’s Talk campaign promotes real-time performance conversations, while QuizWiz and Art Beats foster engagement and camaraderie. The Hi5 Plus App offers gamified recognition and holistic wellness tracking with challenges like Stepathons. Family days, festive celebrations, and care hampers support personal milestones. HR excellence is recognized through HREM Awards (15 businesses, 30 CII assessors) and AHA 2024 (144 applications), evaluating talent acquisition, development, engagement, and system compliance aligned with Lakshya 2026.

nodes.title: Health, Safety and Well-being
nodes.summary: The text covers L&T's commitment to occupational health and safety, emphasizing safety as a core value, especially at high-risk EPC project sites. It highlights that health and safety are material topics extending to all workforce categories, including contract workers. The 'Mission Zero Harm' initiative and the EHS Council, led by the Deputy MD, are described, along with their reporting to the Executive Committee and Board. The Corporate EHS Policy and business unit-specific policies aligned with ISO 45001 and OHSAS are outlined. The EHS Management System's implementation across corporate, business, and site levels is detailed, including the organizational structure from the Board down to site EHS teams.

nodes.title: EHS Plans and Hazard Risk Management
nodes.summary: The text explains that site-specific EHS Plans operationalize the EHS Management System for each work location, tailored to local processes and context. For EPC project sites, EHS planning starts during bidding and design, with the plan finalized before any on-site work. A key element is Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA), which systematically identifies routine and non-routine hazards, assesses OHS risks, and determines control measures. HIRA involves all relevant stakeholders—design and construction engineers, planning teams, EHS personnel, and contract workers—ensuring comprehensive assessment and effective mitigation.

nodes.title: Safety Performance Triangle
nodes.summary: The text presents a Safety Performance Triangle with reactive levels (fatality, reportable lost time injury, lost time injury, dangerous occurrence, near miss) and proactive levels (unsafe conditions, unsafe acts), noting communication and consultation as most effective and least effective. It outlines risk management steps: establishing context, risk assessment (identification, analysis of severity and probability, evaluation as high/medium/low), and risk treatment using the hierarchy of controls (elimination, substitution, engineering controls, administrative controls, PPE) with specific actions. It also describes company-developed applications digitalizing EHS processes to reduce manual effort, integrate data, and generate insights, using machine learning and NLP for actionable inputs, plus AR/VR for immersive training to enhance outcomes for employees and workers.

nodes.title: Workplace Safety Implementation and Contractor Compliance
nodes.summary: The text covers workplace safety implementation and contractor compliance, detailing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for specific work activities and their enforcement during design and execution. It describes a Permit to Work (PTW) system for high-risk activities, and emphasizes that subcontractors and their workforce must strictly adhere to Company EHS policies, which is embedded contractually, with site teams possibly imposing enhanced EHS requirements. It also mentions L&T’s Code of Conduct for Suppliers including health and safety provisions, requiring suppliers to submit a compliance declaration. Finally, it mandates safety induction training for all individuals—employees, contractual workers, or third-party visitors—before site access.

nodes.title: Training, Awareness and Communication
nodes.summary: The text covers how training, awareness, and communication support EHSMS implementation. It details a site-specific EHS training plan for employees and contract workers, covering policies, SOPs, hazard identification, emergency preparedness, non-compliance consequences, and health and safety practices via varied channels. Toolbox Talks by engineers or supervisors address daily risks and SOPs, while specialized training targets high-risk operations like working at heights, confined spaces, and tunnels. Notice boards and warning signs communicate safety information, risks, and precautions. A Communication Matrix maps EHSMS elements, stakeholders, communication modes, and records for systematic, traceable information flow.

nodes.title: Performance Monitoring
nodes.summary: The text covers EHS performance monitoring from site to board level, including daily qualitative and quantitative monitoring, reporting of non-compliance, monthly EHS committee meetings, internal/external audits, incident investigations, and focus on lead indicators. It also details employee mental well-being initiatives: a wellness survey based on physical, social, emotional, and financial pillars leading to a wellness policy, health check-ups, and Aarogya Mela; well-being metrics like training, webinars, screening camps, and counselling services with registration and case numbers; a Mental Health First Aider campaign; World Mental Health Day activities; emotional well-being programs with partners; and other initiatives like the Larsen Memorial Run and Mumbai Sea Bridge Marathon.

nodes.title: R&D initiatives at L&T Construction Research and Testing Centre
nodes.summary: The text covers the L&T Construction Research and Testing Centre (LTCRTC), a DSIR-recognized and NABL-accredited facility in India's private construction sector that tests materials, provides solutions, and conducts R&D. It details four innovations: a Bluetooth Low Energy and AI-based Maturity Meter for concrete strength monitoring that cuts testing costs by 60% and time by 20%; a chloride removal technique using DC current and sacrificial anodes to reduce costs by 70%; Geopolymer Concrete replacing cement with fly ash and GGBS to cut embodied carbon by 60%; Textile-Reinforced Concrete using glass fibre textiles to eliminate steel and reduce carbon footprint by 15-20%; and High-Performance Asphalt Mixes (HiPER) that reduce pavement thickness, cost by 7-10%, virgin aggregates by 25-35%, and carbon footprint by 10-15%.

nodes.title: Innovative Low-Carbon Concrete Solutions: Geopolymer and Textile-Reinforced
nodes.summary: LTCRTC develops Geopolymer Concrete replacing OPC with fly ash and GGBS, activated by alkaline solutions, reducing embodied carbon by ~60% and eliminating water use, suitable for precast applications like sewer lines and housing. It also develops Textile-Reinforced Concrete (TRC) using glass fibre textiles instead of steel, cutting carbon footprint by ~15-20% and reducing weight, used in lift irrigation civil works in Odisha. Both innovations address high embodied carbon in cement and steel, offering sustainable alternatives with improved strength and durability for construction.

nodes.title: High-Performance Asphalt Mixes
nodes.summary: The text addresses rutting in bituminous pavements and introduces High-Performance Asphalt Mixtures (HiPER) for warm and hot climates. LTRCTC developed HiPER through synthetic co-polymers, reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) aggregate replacement, and hard-grade binders. Benefits include reduced pavement thickness, 7-10% cost savings, 25-35% less virgin aggregate use, and a 10-15% lower carbon footprint. HiPER's fatigue resistance extends pavement lifespan and cuts repair and maintenance costs. The mixes are being explored for highway and airport runway projects prone to creep loading and rutting.

nodes.title: Unnati - Integrated Community Development Programme
nodes.summary: Unnati is L&T's flagship integrated rural development programme that starts with watershed management for water security, then uses a four-year phased approach covering health, sanitation, education, and skill-building. Since 2014 it has impacted 30,092 households and treated 44,856 hectares across Rajasthan, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu. In 2022 it expanded to more underserved communities in these states, deepening impact and promoting sustainable rural development. Growth data shows 10,737 households in 2014, 12,545 households and 15,465 hectares by 2022, and 30,092 households and 44,856 hectares by 2024.

nodes.title: Watershed Management
nodes.summary: The text discusses L&T's integrated watershed management approach in India to address water security in rural areas. It combines reviving traditional water structures with new infrastructure for year-round water availability. Interventions target ecologically sensitive areas in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Tamil Nadu, where groundwater decline and poor resource management impact agriculture. Communities implement water and soil conservation measures like check dams, anicuts, gully plugs, contour trenches, and farm bunds, along with indigenous sapling plantations to reduce erosion and improve yields. Village Development Committees sustain efforts through by-laws, maintenance fees, and linking communities to government schemes and markets. This ecosystem-based model enhances water security, agricultural productivity, household incomes, food availability, and economic resilience. The text also includes a before-and-after repair image of Paniyara anicut in Rajasthan and references the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.

nodes.title: Projects launched in FY 2024–25
nodes.summary:
Projects launched in FY 2024–25
The Unnati programme was launched in Pachapalayam, Coimbatore, to address critical challenges such as water scarcity, inadequate sanitation, and agricultural stress in Sultanpet and Kinathukadavu blocks. Designed as a 3.5-year initiative, it aims to benefit around 8,000 people through community-driven interventions focused on water resource management, hygiene and livelihood support.
In Devgaon and Nagzari clusters, the education component of Unnati was introduced to enhance children’s access to quality reading material. This initiative promotes regular reading habits, strengthens literacy and numeracy skills, and improves academic performance.

nodes.title: Agriculture
nodes.summary: L&T's agriculture initiatives support small and marginal farmers through an end-to-end approach covering water and soil conservation, soil testing, crop planning, intercropping, drip irrigation, organic inputs, Farmer Field Schools, kitchen gardens, and horticulture. Case studies from the Unnati programme highlight farming revival and self-reliance. Community volunteers (Krishi Mitras and Vasundhara Sevaks) connect farmers to resources, reaching 25,839 households and training 1,622 farmers. SHGs and FPOs provide credit and market access (305 SHGs, 52 farmer groups). Women are empowered through VDCs and SHGs, and livestock development addresses climate resilience. Sanitation interventions in 11 locations across three states have built 4,456 sanitation units and 2,719 household toilets, making 41 villages open defecation free, with community engagement and monitoring.

nodes.title: Agriculture (intro)
nodes.summary: The text describes L&T's support for Indian farmers, 86% of whom have small or marginal landholdings and face low productivity, limited inputs, rainfall dependency, and poor market access. L&T uses an end-to-end approach across pre-production, production, and post-production. It starts with water availability and soil conservation, then soil testing and moisture retention for multi-seasonal cultivation. Farmers are grouped for seasonal crop planning and introduced to inter- and multi-cropping. Drip irrigation, mulching, and organic input preparation reduce costs and address water scarcity and chemical dependency. Farmer Field Schools and demonstration plots share best practices and build climate resilience. Kitchen gardens and horticulture orchards provide nutritional support and extra income. This strengthens every farming stage, enhancing productivity, reducing input costs, improving incomes, and contributing to food security and long-term sustainability.

nodes.title: Unnati Programme Success Stories: Farming Revival and Self-Reliance
key_items: Shri Pratap Singh – Reviving Farming through Unnati
Ganga & Krishna Gite – From Struggle to Self-Reliance
nodes.summary: The page presents two case studies from the Unnati programme. Shri Pratap Singh returned to his Rajasthan village after 43 years in Mumbai and revived farming with year-round water, adopting sustainable practices through Farmer Field Schools, growing diverse vegetables using natural methods, and earning ₹76,000 by selling seedlings. Ganga and Krishna Gite from Aurangabad overcame struggles, including Krishna's alcoholism, through the programme's soil and water conservation measures. Krishna trained as a Vasundhara Sevak, led community mobilisation, and coordinated with local bodies. Together they adopted improved farming, started a silkworm cocoon unit, planted mulberry and citrus trees, and increased income to nearly ₹3 lakh annually, with ₹6 lakh projected. Both stories highlight transformation and self-reliance.

nodes.title: Krishi Mitras and Vasundhara Sevaks: Bridging Knowledge and Impact
nodes.summary: The text covers L&T's community initiatives: Krishi Mitras and Vasundhara Sevaks train local volunteers to connect farmers with resources and best practices, reaching 25,839 households and training 1,622 farmers. It details support for SHGs and FPOs providing credit and market access, with 305 active SHGs and 52 farmer groups in the Unnati project. nodes.summary: L&T promotes SHGs and FPOs to provide farmers affordable credit, training, government scheme access, and market linkages, with the Unnati project supporting 305 SHGs and 52 farmer groups. VDCs and SHGs empower women through financial inclusion, resource management, and leadership training. nodes.title: Promoting Safe Sanitation: Towards Open Defecation Free Villages
nodes.summary: Open defecation poses health risks and hinders development, requiring infrastructure and cultural change. L&T initiated sanitation interventions in 11 locations across Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Tamil Nadu, focusing on community engagement, hygiene consultations, local leadership, and awareness. Nigrani Samitis monitor sanitation, students serve as Swachhta Doots, and youth receive masonry training. The project has built 4,456 sanitation units, with 2,719 households following suit, making 41 villages ODF. A school sanitation unit was constructed in Brahmangaon Village. A case study details Nikhil's recovery from severe malnutrition via CMAM and MTC. The section also covers rural education challenges and solutions, such as early childhood education, teacher training, and community-managed LRCs, and the ELM at Home initiative that trained mentor mothers to improve early learning, with coverage statistics across Unnati locations.

nodes.title: Health (intro)
nodes.summary: The text outlines health challenges in rural India, including food insecurity, gender norms limiting women's healthcare access, and maternal/child malnutrition. It describes the Unnati programme's goals to break this cycle through nutritional awareness, healthcare access, and behavioral change. Community volunteers, VDCs, and SHGs lead initiatives on diet, kitchen gardening, hygiene, and Anganwadi awareness, resulting in increased health-seeking behavior. The programme also empowers communities to advocate for supply-side improvements. L&T's holistic approach includes improving food security via agriculture, horticulture, and livestock. nodes.title: Nikhil’s Recovery from Malnutrition
nodes.summary: The text describes one-year-old Nikhil from Koyla village who was identified with severe malnutrition during a home visit by Bal Sakhi Sohna Devi. Weighing 5.7 kg and measuring 68 cm, he was enrolled in a CMAM camp, where medical staff recommended admission to the MTC for specialized care. Despite initial hesitation, Sohna Devi reassured the family and they agreed to 15 days of treatment at the MTC in Kankroli. Afterwards, Nikhil was re-enrolled in the CMAM camp, receiving therapeutic food and medicines, while his mother received nutrition training. Nikhil recovered remarkably, now weighing 7.3 kg and thriving, thanks to the support of Sohna Devi and his mother. The text ends with document section headings: Management Discussion and Analysis, Integrated Report, Statutory Reports, and Financial Statements.

nodes.title: Challenges and Solutions in Rural Education
nodes.summary: India's rural education faces high dropout rates, poor learning outcomes, inadequate infrastructure, teacher shortages, language barriers, gender disparities, and limited parental involvement due to low parental education. Solutions include strengthening early childhood education in Anganwadis, teacher training, providing Teaching and Learning Materials, supplementary literacy and numeracy classes, training parents to support learning, and establishing mobile libraries and Learning Resource Centres (LRCs) managed by community volunteers and handed over to the community for sustainability.

nodes.title: Empowering Mothers through the ELM at Home Initiative
nodes.summary: The ELM at Home initiative in Rajasthan trained 65 mentor mothers to teach young children, with Hemlata's story illustrating community impact. A rapid assessment in 12 villages revealed gaps in reading and mathematics, leading to an intervention for children aged 6-14. Coverage under Unnati in five locations is detailed with statistics on water, agriculture, health, livestock, livelihoods, institution building, and capacity building.

Education
L&T’s educational initiatives aim to drive social progress and inclusive development in India’s education system. These efforts include improving infrastructure in under-resourced rural, peri-urban and urban schools, establishing community learning centres, enhancing teacher skills and promoting community monitoring systems. Integrating STEM pedagogy with existing science and mathematics curricula requires comprehensive teacher training to engage students in STEM effectively.

nodes.title: Early Childhood Support
nodes.summary: The text describes L&T's preschool initiative in Mumbai's low-income areas, operating 87 Balwadis for 10 months, serving 4,302 children to prepare them for primary school through emotional, cognitive, language, and sensory-motor development. It empowers local women by training them as teachers and includes teacher training, learning assessments, home visits, and parental involvement, resulting in a 43% average skill improvement. A chart shows Classroom Learning Evaluation (CLE) scores from July 2024 to March 2025 across physical, language, cognitive, and socio-emotional development. A case study of Mamata Chaudhary and her daughter Hansika illustrates the program's impact: Hansika thrived in play-based learning, and Mamata engaged through workshops, mothers' groups, and WhatsApp, supporting Hansika's foundational learning.

nodes.title: Learning Enhancement through the School Partnership Programme
nodes.summary: L&T's School Partnership Programme in nine Powai, Mumbai municipal primary schools enhances foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN) through learner-led interactive methods, reaching 2,965 children. Initiatives include Reading Promotion and Home Lending to boost linguistic skills. Results show 19% improvement in literacy, 44% in numeracy, 46% in reading levels, and 27% in language development via the library initiative. The Reading Promotion Programme Assessment presents baseline (July 2024) and endline (February 2025) data across six reading levels (L1-L6), detailing percentages of children at each level, from cannot read to reading complex sentences with speed and comprehension.

nodes.title: Jyoti – STEM Education Initiative
nodes.summary: The Jyoti STEM Education Initiative section covers a Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra program for grades 6-8 using digital infrastructure, teacher training (200 teachers, 208 in innovation contest), hands-on models, activity-based learning, Edu-Reels, robotics, space kits, an Entrepreneurs Bootcamp (450 students, 75 solutions), science fairs, STEM Innovation and Learning Centres, and ABL sessions, with outcomes including 80% easier teaching, 95% better conceptual clarity, 85% increased parent-noticed interest, 83% improved math/science grades, and 89% strong science interest, plus a DIET principal quote and grade 6-8 baseline/endline chart; it highlights Jyoti STEM Labs and the Life App enabling projects like water purification and rockets, L&T's Community Learning Centres (41 Mumbai, 10 Chennai, 3,000+ children) providing remedial literacy/numeracy; and transformation stories of Suraj and Anjali Narsing Tadale.

nodes.title: Jyoti – STEM Education Initiative (intro)
nodes.summary: Project Jyoti is a STEM education initiative for grades 6-8 in government schools across Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra, aiming to bridge educational disparities through digital infrastructure, teacher training, hands-on models, and activity-based learning (ABL). It includes teacher training (200 teachers trained, 68 students created 24 models), Edu-Reels, robotics and space kits, an Entrepreneurs Bootcamp, science fairs, STEM Innovation and Learning Centres (SILC), a Teacher Innovation Contest (208 teachers from 123 schools), and ABL sessions using STEM TLM. Outcomes: 80% of teachers find teaching easier, 95% of students show better conceptual clarity, 85% of parents notice increased interest, 83% improved grades in math and science, and 89% express strong interest in science. A quote from a DIET principal and a subject-wise average percentage chart comparing baseline and endline for grades 6-8 in science and mathematics are also included.

nodes.title: Sparking Scientific Curiosity Through Jyoti STEM Labs
nodes.summary: The text highlights Jyoti STEM Labs enabling student Kanishka to engage with science through interactive tools, the Life App, and hands-on projects like water purification systems and rockets. It covers the Young Entrepreneurs Finale 2025, where 450 students from 75 schools showcased 75 innovative solutions, following an 18-hour Design Thinking workshop and teacher training, with L&T mentorship. Additionally, it describes L&T’s Community Learning Centres providing remedial support for foundational literacy and numeracy to primary students through after-school sessions, currently operating 41 centres in Mumbai and 10 in Chennai, benefiting over 3,000 children with measurable learning improvements.

nodes.title: Suraj’s Journey from Struggling Student to Confident Learner
nodes.summary: The text narrates Suraj's transformation from a struggling 5th-grade student facing economic hardship, limited academic support, and low self-esteem to a confident learner. Initially unable to read or do basic math and hesitant to ask questions, his turning point came through L&T's Community Learning Centre programme, which used hands-on activities and real-life applications. Within four months, his communication improved; over two years, he achieved significant academic gains in math and language and developed leadership through public speaking and dance. The story highlights the impact of holistic, inclusive education in unlocking potential.

nodes.title: Anjali Narsing Tadale – From Academic Struggles to Aspiring Nurse
key_items: Reflecting on her experience, Anjali shares, “The interactive teaching methods made learning exciting and practical.”
nodes.summary: Anjali Narsing Tadale's journey from a financially constrained background and academic struggles in mathematics and language due to poor educational support and rote learning to thriving at L&T's Community Learning Centre, where interactive, concept-focused methods built her confidence, questioning, and participation. She discovered public speaking and singing talents, took leadership roles, completed 12th grade science, and now pursues General Nursing and Midwifery while working part-time. Her story illustrates how equitable education and supportive ecosystems can transform a student's life trajectory.

nodes.title: Self-Learning Classes
nodes.summary:
Self-Learning Classes
As part of the broader education programme, self-learning groups have been established for children in Grades 6 to 8, encouraging peer collaboration and independent study. On average, 131 children participate monthly, forming groups of five that meet at least once a week. These sessions run for 23 days each month and involve working through instructional materials and practice exercises in a collaborative setting. This model supports academic learning and fosters teamwork, critical thinking and self-discipline among children. A notable ripple effect of the intervention is the increased involvement of the local elderly population, who now offer their homes as safe, quiet learning spaces. Many of them also take an active interest in the children’s progress by monitoring sessions and providing encouragement.

nodes.title: Supporting Schools through Infrastructure Development
key_items: Transforming a Tribal School in Nigade Village, Pune
Sustainable Water Access in Chak Dhani, Nagaur, Rajasthan
nodes.summary: L&T supports under-resourced government schools by building and renovating infrastructure, supplying furniture, lab equipment, libraries, and digital tools, and upgrading facilities with solar power and clean water. It provides learning materials and uniforms to low-income students. Case studies detail transforming a tribal school in Nigade with new classrooms, solar power, and water filtration, and implementing rainwater harvesting in a Rajasthan desert school. The education programme engages principals, teachers, and students, promotes STEM via the Jyoti programme, strengthens School Management Committees, educates parents, and collaborates with government. Statistics cover interventions, schools, and students. L&T also operates Community Health Centres and Mobile Health Units across three states, offering primary care, outreach, and integration with national health programmes.

nodes.title: Cancer Care Services

The text also profiles Raginiben Bakkariya, a kidney failure patient receiving free dialysis at L&T Health and Dialysis Centre in Surat under a national program, and Mr. Sivaraja, a farmer with high blood pressure aided by mobile health units and a Tamil Nadu home-care initiative. These cases illustrate collaborative healthcare access and improved rural outcomes.

nodes.title: Skill Development
nodes.summary: L&T addresses India's construction skill gap through CSTIs since 1995, offering NSQF-aligned training with 80% hands-on learning, NCVT certification, and soft skills, including gender inclusivity efforts. Key stats: 12,594 CSTI trainees with 72% placement and ₹17,800 average salary; 121 Multi-Skill Training Centre trainees; 2,466 in other courses; and 1,889 women trained. The Skill Trainers Academy in Mumbai, run with MSDE and NSDC, trains high-calibre trainers. The section shares Laxmi Murmu's inspiring story, covers an impact assessment of 27 CSR projects reaching 5.5 lakh beneficiaries across skilling, education, health, and WASH, and details employee volunteering (9,590 volunteers) and the Young Science Leader initiative with 126 science models by 378 students. Future plans include two new CSTIs and promoting STEM education.

nodes.title: Skill Development (intro)
nodes.summary: L&T addresses India's construction skill gap by running Construction Skills Training Institutes (CSTIs) since 1995 across nine locations, offering training in 14+ trades with 80% hands-on learning, NSQF-aligned curricula, NCVT certification, and soft skills. The text covers gender inclusivity efforts, including training and placing women, and presents key stats: 12,594 CSTI trainees with a 72% placement rate and ₹17,800 average monthly salary, plus 121 Multi-Skill Training Centre trainees and 2,466 in other vocational courses. It also describes L&T's Skill Trainers Academy in Mumbai, run with the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and NSDC, training high-calibre trainers, and highlights contributions to youth employability and national infrastructure growth.

nodes.title: Story of Laxmi Murmu, who defied societal norms
nodes.summary: The text recounts Laxmi Murmu's journey from a disadvantaged background in Odisha to becoming a data operator and office assistant in Rajasthan after vocational training, highlighting her role in inspiring her community and her aspiration to train others. It also notes that 1,889 women were trained through skill development initiatives. Additionally, it describes L&T's Skill Trainers Academy in Maharashtra, established in 2021, which enhances trainer capabilities through its Training of Trainers programme, has trained 835 trainers in the past year, and is recognized as an Exclusive Centre by CSDCI, contributing to social and relationship capital.

nodes.title: Impact Assessment of CSR Projects

It lists government schemes linked to CSR interventions, and details L&T's initiatives in toilets, WASH awareness, watershed development, STEM education, health centres, and Anganwadi support. It describes the L&T-eering employee volunteering initiative with 9,590 volunteers, the Young Science Leader initiative in Gujarat including mentoring, workshops, and a science exhibition, and future plans for new Construction Skills Training Institutes and enhanced STEM education.

nodes.title: L&T Employee Volunteering and YSL Science Initiative
nodes.summary: The page covers L&T's employee volunteering culture with 9,590 volunteers engaged in education, healthcare, and environmental initiatives in FY 2024-25. Overall, 59 L&Teers contributed 1,611 volunteer hours to promote STEM education.

nodes.title: Student Engagement
nodes.summary: The text covers student engagement through mentoring by 32 L&Teers from November to December 2024, including online and offline support in model enhancement, presentation, and coaching, following interactive sessions at two schools. It outlines future plans: establishing two new Construction Skills Training Institutes (CSTIs) to expand youth access to skill development and strengthen existing CSTIs as Centres of Excellence, addressing a 4 million annual skilled worker shortage in India's construction sector, which contributes 9% to GDP and employs 50 million, with a projected need for 91 million skilled workers by 2030. Additionally, it highlights promoting STEM education in government schools by engaging parents and the community for a supportive ecosystem and long-term sustainability.
